companies.description: connectFirst Credit Union is a member-owned, cooperative (Schedule-equivalent provincial credit union) financial institution headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, formed on May 3, 2021 by amalgamating four Alberta credit unions (First Calgary Financial, Chinook Financial, Mountain View Financial, and Legacy Financial). At its peak it held over CAD $6 billion in assets under administration and served more than 128,000 members across 41 branches in Central and Southern Alberta, offering retail, commercial, agricultural, and dealer-services banking. Members voted in November 2023 to merge with Servus Credit Union; the legal amalgamation closed May 1, 2024 as "Connect First and Servus Credit Union Ltd." (~CAD $29.3B assets, 600,000+ members), and the unified brand realigned to Servus Credit Union in January 2025 — the connectfirstcu.com domain now 301-redirects to servus.ca. Its open-finance posture is honest and typical of a Canadian credit union: no first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI, digital banking delivered via the Celero Xpress platform (powered by ebankIT) with core/banking-tech through the Central 1 / Celero cooperative ecosystem, and third-party consumer data access available only through aggregators (Plaid coverage confirmed). Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC-overseen) is legislated but not yet operational, so no mandated open-banking API exists.

companies.name: Equifax
companies.description: Equifax is a consumer credit reporting agency that collects and aggregates information on individuals' credit history, including borrowing and repayment habits. This information is used by lenders and creditors to assess creditworthiness and make decisions about extending credit. Equifax also offers identity theft protection, credit monitoring, and fraud detection services, plus analytics and consulting offerings to help businesses manage risk.

companies.name: Kredete
companies.description: Kredete is an intelligent global finance app for diaspora and emerging-market communities, founded in 2022 and operating across four continents. It moves money across 60+ markets at the mid-market rate with settlement in about ten seconds, issues US dollar Visa cards accepted in 170+ countries, opens multi-currency accounts in the customer's own name, pays yield on US dollar savings held through partner US chartered institutions, and reports rent and repayment history to the major US credit bureaus so customers build a US credit file. Kredete for Business adds multi-currency operating accounts, corporate cards, FedWire routing, payroll, and invoicing. An in-app agent runs these actions on the customer's behalf with confirmation. Kredete is a financial technology company, not a bank; remittance and banking services are provided by partner US licensed financial institutions. Backed by Partech and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass Kredete publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API description.

companies.name: Discover Financial Services
companies.description: Discover Financial Services is a US direct bank and payments company that owns the Discover Network, the PULSE debit network, and Diners Club International. Its Discover Global Network (DGN) developer program exposes a partner-gated developer center with interactive OpenAPI documentation for card-network products — EMV 3-D Secure (ProtectBuy), Secure Remote Commerce / Click to Pay, Stored Token Services (tokenization), and Discover Deliver push payments. Consumer account-data access is delivered through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity) rather than a first-party retail-banking API.

companies.name: ANNA Money
companies.description: ANNA Money (a trading name of Absolutely No Nonsense Admin Ltd, company number 10149389, Cardiff, a subsidiary of ANNA Holdings Ltd) is a UK digital business account and tax app for freelancers, startups, and small businesses, positioned as a challenger to the high-street banks. ANNA is not a bank but an e-money proposition: its Mastercard and e-money services are issued by PayrNet Limited, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for electronic money service activities (FCA FRN 900594), and its Account Information Services are provided under agency of TrueLayer (FCA FRN 901096). Within UK Open Banking, ANNA is a consumer / third-party provider (TPP) rather than an account-holding ASPSP or a CMA9 mandated bank - it uses TrueLayer's Data and Payments APIs for external account aggregation, automatic VAT calculation, and QR-code "pay by bank" collection. ANNA publishes no public developer portal, no Open Data API, and no OBIE Read/Write (AIS/PIS/CBPII) API surface of its own; its public GitHub organisation hosts open-source engineering tooling (asyncio, aiohttp, and Postgres libraries) rather than product APIs.

companies.name: BioCatch
companies.description: BioCatch is a financial-fraud and financial-crime prevention platform that uses behavioral intelligence — analyzing how people physically interact with their devices — to detect threats that static rules and device recognition miss. The platform monitors account-opening fraud, account takeover, social-engineering scams, mule accounts, and money-laundering networks across the digital banking session. Marquee products include BioCatch Connect (the core telemetry and behavioral-analysis platform), Scams360, BioCatch Trust (an inter-bank fraud intelligence network), DeviceIQ / DeviceIQai device-trust assessment, mule and account-takeover protection, and Strong Customer Authentication. Integration is delivered under contract through platform components such as the Push API, Align SDK, Link, Fuse, the Insights Query Engine, and Rule Manager; developer documentation lives behind a login at docs.biocatch.com rather than a public developer portal. BioCatch serves 350+ global retail banks, protects over 680 million accounts, and analyzes roughly 18 billion sessions monthly.

companies.name: Credi2
companies.description: Credi2 GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based fintech that operates a white-label, cloud-native embedded lending platform enabling banks, card issuers, and merchants to launch Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and installment financing products under their own brand. The modular platform covers five financing products - pay per invoice (14-day BNPL), split pay (3-12 month installments up to EUR 5,000), installment loans (up to EUR 50,000 over 84 months), revolving credit lines, and subscription financing - and handles the full lifecycle including core banking operations, credit and risk management, servicing, and collections. Use cases span eCommerce and point-of-sale financing, subscription payments, installment-on-cards, and cash loans, with omni-channel integration and go-live in weeks. Credi2 is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified and is backed by Speedinvest.

companies.name: Esusu
companies.description: Esusu is a financial technology company that turns rent payments into credit history. Founded in 2018 by Abbey Wemimo and Samir Goel and headquartered in New York City, Esusu reports on-time rental payments to the three major credit bureaus (Equifax, TransUnion, and Experian) so renters can build and improve their credit scores. The platform serves renters, property owners and managers, employers, banks, and fintechs with rent reporting, credit building, rent relief, marketplace rewards, and income, identity, and SSN verification. For partners, Esusu offers embedded rent-reporting APIs, UI tools, and SDKs (behind a sandbox and self-service docs) so banks and fintechs can distribute rent reporting as a service. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Serena Ventures, Esusu reached a $1.2 billion valuation in 2025 and reports across millions of rental units in all 50 US states.

companies.name: Every
companies.description: Every is an AI-native, all-in-one back-office and finance platform built for startups, unifying incorporation, business banking and cards, treasury and cash management, global payroll, HR and benefits, AI-assisted bookkeeping, and startup tax preparation (including R&D tax credits) into a single system. It offers free Delaware C-corp formation, business checking with cashback debit cards, treasury-bill and money-market investing, and bundled per-stage plans for new founders through established startups. Backed by Redpoint Ventures. Every does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, commercial, and domain-security surface.

companies.name: Nu (Nubank)
companies.description: Nu Holdings (Nubank) is Latin America's largest digital bank, with tens of millions of customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Its core product surface - credit card, account, lending, investments, and insurance - is consumer-facing through the Nu mobile app, and Nubank does not publish a general-purpose public developer portal. Nubank participates in Brazil's Open Finance (Open Banking Brasil) regime, which standardises consent-driven access to account, transaction, and payment-initiation APIs for authorised third parties; Nubank's Open Finance endpoints are registered with the Brazilian Central Bank's directory. For merchant acceptance, Nubank operates NuPay for Business, a REST API for checkout payments, refunds, OAuth2/CIBA-based authorization, beneficiary management, and webhook event notifications, hosted at api.spinpay.com.br.

companies.name: Trade Republic
companies.description: Trade Republic is a Berlin-based digital bank and Europe's largest savings platform, offering commission-optimized trading of stocks, ETFs, derivatives, and crypto, ETF and stock savings plans, interest on uninvested cash, and a Visa card. Trade Republic Bank GmbH holds a full German banking license and serves customers across European markets. The company publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or first-party SDKs — its mobile and web apps run on a private WebSocket-based backend (api.traderepublic.com) that a community ecosystem of unofficial clients has grown around.

companies.name: Canadian Tire Bank
companies.description: Canadian Tire Bank (operating as Canadian Tire Financial Services) is a federally regulated Schedule I bank, wholly owned by Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited and federally chartered in 2003. Headquartered in Oakville, Ontario with operations in St. Catharines and Welland, the bank is the financial-services arm of one of Canada's best-known retailers. It issues the Triangle Mastercard, Triangle World Mastercard, Triangle World Elite Mastercard, Gas Advantage and Cash Advantage Mastercards, and offers high-interest savings accounts and GICs, all tied to the Triangle Rewards loyalty program. On open finance, the bank exposes no first-party public developer API or banking API portal. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer data access today is voluntary and aggregator-based — Canadian Tire Bank card and account data is reached through aggregators such as Finicity (by Mastercard), Flinks and Plaid rather than a first-party API. The cantire.com developer portal is run by the retail parent Canadian Tire Corporation, not the bank, is gated behind sign-in, and its TLS certificate expired in February 2026.

companies.name: Coast Capital Savings
companies.description: Coast Capital Savings is a member-owned financial co-operative headquartered in Surrey, British Columbia, serving over 600,000 members across roughly 45 branches. On November 1, 2018 it became Canada's first British Columbia-based federal credit union (regulated federally rather than provincially), and in May 2026 it completed a merger with Prospera Credit Union. With approximately $21.9 billion CAD in total assets it is one of Canada's largest credit unions. As a cooperative credit union rather than a Schedule I/II bank, Coast Capital operates within Canada's voluntary and still-fragmented open-finance landscape: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework legislated under Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer, is not yet operational. Coast Capital publishes NO public first-party developer portal or documented API; consumer financial-data access today is aggregator-mediated (e.g. Plaid) via screen-scraping/credential-based connections rather than a first-party API.

companies.name: Cross River Bank
companies.description: Cross River Bank is an FDIC-insured chartered bank that operates as a sponsor bank and banking-as-a-service (BaaS) provider for fintech companies, embedded-finance platforms, and crypto / stablecoin issuers. The product surface is delivered through the Cross River Operating System (COS) - a proprietary API-driven banking core with real-time subledger generation - and includes accounts, ACH and Same-Day ACH, RTP and FedNow instant payments, wires, card issuing and processing (Visa / Mastercard), merchant acquiring, stablecoin rails, consumer and SMB lending, and capital markets / loan participation services. API access is gated behind a partner onboarding process; documentation and sandbox are at docs.crossriver.com.

companies.name: Wintrust Financial
companies.description: Wintrust Financial Corporation is a Rosemont, Illinois-based financial holding company operating a network of chartered community banks (Wintrust Bank, N.A. and its affiliates) primarily across Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana and Florida, plus specialty lending, wealth management and mortgage businesses. Wintrust does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; its programmatic surface is delivered through commercial treasury management. Wintrust describes "API banking" that connects businesses directly to its secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) for account balance and activity reporting, payment files (Positive Pay, ACH, wires, EDI, lockbox) and data-format translation (NACHA, EDI 820, BAI2). Consumer and small-business account data is reachable to third parties through open-banking aggregators — Plaid is the confirmed aggregator supporting Wintrust / iBusinessBanking access.

companies.name: HighRadius
companies.description: HighRadius is an AI-powered autonomous finance platform for the Office of the CFO, automating the Order-to-Cash (O2C), Record-to-Report (R2R), Accounts Payable (AP), and Treasury processes with a network of orchestrated AI agents. The platform covers invoicing, collections, cash application, deductions, credit, dispute management, financial close, reconciliation, consolidation, and cash forecasting. HighRadius serves 1,500+ enterprise customers and ships pre-built integrations with 50+ ERPs and systems including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, and NetSuite. Integration is delivered through those pre-built ERP connectors and partner engagements rather than a public self-serve developer API; the company publishes a Trust Center documenting SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and GDPR posture.

companies.name: Stessa
companies.description: Stessa is a financial reporting, accounting, and management platform for rental property owners and small-to-mid-size landlords, headquartered in San Francisco and operated as a brand of Roofstock alongside Mynd and RentPrep. The platform helps owners track unlimited properties and portfolios with automated bank and credit card feeds, transaction categorization, mileage tracking, receipt scanning, Schedule E-ready tax reporting, online rent collection, tenant screening through RentPrep, e-signature leasing with 50+ legal templates, maintenance request tracking, and property-specific Stessa Cash Management accounts with high-yield APY and FDIC insurance up to $3M per entity. Stessa is delivered as a web app and iOS/Android mobile apps with three tiers — Essentials (free), Manage, and Pro — and serves more than 350,000 landlords. Bank, credit card, and payment data flows in through aggregator partners (Plaid-style open banking) rather than a public Stessa API, and the only developer-facing GitHub presence is an org with a handful of forked Ruby and Vue.js utilities. There is no public Stessa REST API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no published webhooks; the Stessa community has open feature requests for a public API to pull reports and transactions, but none has shipped.

companies.name: HSBC USA
companies.description: HSBC USA is the United States arm of HSBC Holdings plc, operating principally through HSBC Bank USA, N.A., a nationally chartered bank supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). After exiting mass-market domestic retail banking in 2022 — selling its East Coast branches and national online deposit business to Citizens and its West Coast branches to Cathay Bank — HSBC refocused its US operations on global wholesale, commercial and corporate banking, global banking and markets, and wealth management for internationally connected clients. On the open-finance front, HSBC USA does not publish a US-specific first-party developer program; public API access is provided through HSBC's group-wide corporate and institutional Developer Portal (developer.hsbc.com), whose transaction-banking API products serve US wholesale clients but require registration and login to reach the actual API reference and specifications. There is no publicly downloadable OpenAPI, and consumer-permissioned data access for remaining US accounts is mediated through third-party aggregators rather than a documented first-party consumer data-sharing API.

companies.name: Arc
companies.description: Arc is an intelligent cash management platform for technology companies that consolidates business banking, treasury, debt capital, and AI-powered financial services into a single dashboard. Customers can sweep idle cash into yield-bearing accounts, manage liquidity across multiple accounts, raise debt capital, and access AI tooling for financial operations. Arc also offers a Global Treasury product that lets qualifying startups invest in US Treasury Bills as non-US entities while safeguarding funds in US brokerage accounts. The platform is primarily delivered through a hosted web application rather than a public REST API, and integrations are coordinated through Arc's solutions and customer success teams. Arc is positioned as a unified financial operating system for venture-backed and growth-stage technology businesses.

companies.name: FintechOS
companies.description: FintechOS is an AI-powered financial product operations platform that enables banks, lenders, and insurers to configure, price, launch, and manage financial products with reduced dependency on legacy core systems. The platform combines unified product operations, agentic workflow orchestration, and governed AI to streamline origination, servicing, underwriting, and compliance across banking and insurance. It exposes a low-code development environment with Server SDK and Client SDK layers and REST APIs, documented at docs.fintechos.com, with a gated developer community and an academy for onboarding. Founded in Romania with headquarters in the United Kingdom, FintechOS is a portfolio company of Earlybird and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Baselane
companies.description: Baselane is an all-in-one financial platform (financial operating system) for independent landlords and real estate investors, combining FDIC-insured landlord banking, automated rent collection, bookkeeping and expense tracking, analytics and reporting, and cash-flow tools in a single product. Banking services are provided through partner Thread Bank, and account connectivity to external banks is powered by Plaid. Baselane is a consumer/SMB fintech application (web and mobile apps) rather than an API platform: it publishes no first-party public developer API, developer portal, or API reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Sector: fintech / proptech.

companies.name: Step
companies.description: Step is an all-in-one mobile banking platform built for teens, young adults, and families. The Step Visa Card is a secured card that builds credit history reported to Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion, and teens can begin building credit before they turn 18 through parent-managed accounts. Step also offers savings rewards, cashback with partner brands, EarlyPay paycheck advances up to $250, commission-free stock investing powered by DriveWealth, early direct deposit, and the Money 101 financial education hub. Banking services are provided by partner Evolve Bank & Trust, Member FDIC. Founded in 2018 in Palo Alto by CJ MacDonald and Alexey Kalinichenko, backed by General Catalyst, and acquired by Beast Industries. Step publishes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to a consumer service status page and a site llms.txt.

companies.name: Sumeria
companies.description: Sumeria is a French fintech and mobile-first banking service created by Lydia Solutions in 2024 as a consumer spinoff of the Lydia payment app. It offers free online banking accounts with automatic expense categorization, thematic sub-accounts for budgeting and savings, virtual and physical debit cards with no foreign-exchange fees, an interest-bearing balance, and an AI assistant named Sia for account management and financial guidance. Sumeria is a business-to-consumer banking product; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time, so this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

companies.name: UNest
companies.description: UNest is a Los Angeles-based fintech app that helps parents and families save and invest for their children's futures through UTMA/UGMA custodial investment accounts, with brand rewards contributions, gifting, financial literacy content, and term life insurance offered through Ladder. UNest Advisers, LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, with brokerage through UNest Securities, LLC (FINRA/SIPC) and clearing through Apex Clearing. The company is a consumer mobile-app business and publishes no public developer API, though its site ships a real llms.txt. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Vancity Community Investment Bank
companies.description: Vancity Community Investment Bank (VCIB) is a federally regulated Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Vancouver City Savings Credit Union (Vancity), Canada's largest community credit union. Established to carry the cooperative "community-first" finance model into the national banking system, VCIB is a values-driven, Certified B Corporation and CDIC member that provides impact-focused commercial banking - commercial real estate and affordable-housing lending, clean-energy and green-building finance, social-enterprise banking, Impact GICs, high-interest savings, and business Visa products - to organizations driving social, economic, and environmental change. As a small impact/commercial bank rather than one of the Big Six, VCIB operates no public developer portal, exposes no first-party developer API, and publishes no downloadable API specifications. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement under the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, is not yet operational, so any third-party access to VCIB customer data today would be voluntary and aggregator-mediated rather than via a documented open API.

companies.name: Heard
companies.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.

companies.name: TopKey
companies.description: TopKey is an AI-powered financial operating system purpose-built for professional short-term rental, vacation rental, and long-term rental property managers running 50-5,000+ units. It automates property-level and owner-level expense management, corporate and bring-your-own cards (BYOC), bill pay / AP, banking through partner banks (Thread Bank, Member FDIC), AI-assisted accounting, inventory, invoicing, work-order expense tracking, and revenue reconciliation. TopKey integrates deeply with property management systems (Guesty, Hostaway, OwnerRez, Streamline, Track, Hostfully) and accounting software (QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite). Backed by a16z and Felicis. TopKey consumes partner APIs for its integrations but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time; it ships a product help center and a machine-readable llms.txt.

companies.name: Grandhood
companies.description: Grandhood is a Danish digital pension provider that lets companies set up and run a modern workplace (company) pension scheme entirely online, without the traditional adviser meetings and paperwork. Employers register with MitID, invite employees, and activate a plan; employees enroll, get built-in digital pension counselling, choose an investment profile, consolidate scattered pension savings, and see real-time savings, returns, and insurance coverage in the Grandhood mobile app. Pensions bundle both long-term savings and present-day insurance protection. Pricing is a simple fixed monthly amount per employee (65-95 DKK/month) plus investment costs, with no deposit-percentage fees and free pension advice. The underlying pension administration is backed by Velliv, Denmark's third-largest pension company. Grandhood is based in Copenhagen (Esplanaden 14B, 1263 København K; CVR 44147750) and is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. Grandhood publishes consumer web and mobile-app products; it does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Hopper
companies.description: Hopper is a travel marketplace and fintech, best known for consumer flight, hotel, car, and homes booking with fintech ancillaries such as Price Freeze, Cancel for Any Reason, and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason. Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) is the B2B arm that exposes Hopper's e-commerce (Stays, Cars, Packages), fintech ancillaries, loyalty portals, and HTS Assist agentic AI to banks, airlines, and travel providers including Capital One, Air Canada, Virgin Australia, Tripadvisor, Frontier, Wizz Air, and Porter.

companies.name: Knight Fintech
companies.description: Knight Fintech is a Mumbai-based banking technology company that sells digital lending infrastructure to Indian banks and NBFCs. It positions itself as "India's leading digital lending infrastructure platform", stating it powers 500+ financial institutions across co-lending, digital lending, treasury management, supply chain finance, embedded finance and credit line on UPI, alongside a Knight Aurix product line. The company describes its approach as cloud-first, API-driven middleware that integrates with legacy core banking systems without displacing them. It is enterprise sales-led: there is no public developer portal, no published API documentation, no SDKs and no self-service signup — evaluation runs through a scheduled demo.

companies.name: Raisin
companies.description: Raisin is a fintech savings and investment marketplace that gives consumers access to high-yield savings accounts, CDs, and cash deposit products from a network of banks and credit unions through a single account and login. Founded in Berlin (originally as WeltSparen / SavingGlobal) and operating in the US, Germany, and across Europe, Raisin connects more than one million customers with partner banks, handling onboarding, KYC, account management, and deposit brokerage. Its sister entity Raisin Bank provides a Banking-as-a-Service platform for fintechs. Raisin exposes no public, self-serve developer API or documentation portal; integrations are partner-only and its consumer surface is web and mobile apps. Backed by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio lead.

companies.name: Rho
companies.description: Rho is an all-in-one finance platform for businesses that combines business banking, treasury, corporate cards, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, and automated month-end close. Customers get a business checking account with high FDIC sweep insurance, a yield-bearing treasury product, corporate cards with cash back, and zero-fee bill pay, all reconciled against connected accounting systems. Rho serves startups, small businesses, enterprises, accountants, banks, and consumer brands, with no per-seat fees. The platform exposes APIs for use cases such as vendor onboarding and virtual card issuance so partners can embed Rho capabilities into their own portals. Native integrations exist for QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

companies.name: Ziro
companies.description: Zíro (somosziro.com) is a Colombian fintech that provides interest-free credit for small retailers in the traditional commerce channel. Its platform lets distributors and manufacturers extend "crédito sin intereses" to the small shops they supply, while the supplier receives guaranteed payment and Zíro assumes the credit risk. The service bundles identity verification (Colombian cédula), automated credit evaluation, and fraud prevention into the ordering flow. Zíro is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes only a public marketing site and a customer-facing credit application (an Angular SPA at creditos.somosziro.com); no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or MCP server was found. The api.somosziro.com host exists but responds 403 (internal, not publicly documented).

companies.name: Curve
companies.description: Curve is a London-based fintech, founded in 2015 by Shachar Bialick, that consolidates multiple debit and credit cards into a single smart card and mobile wallet. Its "over-the-top" banking platform lets customers spend from any linked Mastercard or Visa card, switch the funding source of a past purchase up to 120 days later with "Go Back in Time", avoid foreign-exchange fees, earn cashback, and pay in instalments with Curve Flex. Premium tiers (Curve Pay X / Pro / Pro+) add insurance, lounge access, and richer rewards. Curve is backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest among others. Curve does not publish a public developer API — it acts as an open-banking consumer to aggregate customer account balances rather than exposing a provider API.

companies.name: FeezBack
companies.description: FeezBack is an Israeli open-banking fintech, founded in 2016, that builds the technological infrastructure and consumer products enabling financial players to compete in Israel's open-banking ecosystem. Its products cover account-to- account payment initiation (direct bank payments with no card-processing fees integrated into sales and point-of-sale flows), aggregated financial data for underwriting and risk assessment, and financial analysis for investment portfolio and risk allocation. FeezBack holds a Bank of Israel financial information service provider (AIS) license and a payment initiation (PIS) approval, and is ISO 27001 certified for information security. The company describes an API-based integration model for partners but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Monese
companies.description: Monese is a London-founded fintech that provides mobile money accounts to consumers across Europe. Operating as a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) rather than a traditional bank, Monese lets over two million users open an account in minutes and then spend, send, and save money directly from a smartphone app. Its product surface covers multi-currency and local accounts, international money transfers, physical and virtual debit cards, budgeting and savings tools, and credit-building features. Monese is a consumer-facing mobile application and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Brim Financial
companies.description: Brim Financial is a Toronto-based Canadian fintech (founded 2017) that operates a fully-integrated, API-first credit-card Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS). It is not a chartered Schedule I or Schedule II bank; it describes itself as the only fintech in North America licensed to issue credit cards, and it delivers Credit-Cards-as-a-Service (CCaaS), loyalty/rewards, BNPL, and money-movement infrastructure to banks, credit unions, fintechs, and large brands (clients include Manulife Bank, Laurentian Bank, Canadian Western Bank, Affinity Credit Union, and Air France-KLM). Brim is registered under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) to Bank of Canada standards and was admitted to Payments Canada as a payment service provider, and has partnered with Mastercard to embed open-banking capabilities. Although Brim markets a comprehensive API-first platform, that API is delivered to enterprise/embedded-finance partners through a commercial onboarding relationship: as of this review there is no public, self-serve first-party developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no operational consumer-driven-banking (open-banking) API, consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-live open-finance framework.

companies.name: Oradian
companies.description: Oradian is an AI-native, cloud-based core banking platform that helps banks, lenders, microfinance institutions, and fintechs in Asia, Africa, and Europe replace legacy core systems and launch, operate, and scale modern banking services from the cloud. Its product, Instafin, is built API-first around an open data model, an extensible architecture, and a native Model Context Protocol surface, exposing capabilities such as ledgers, transactions, deposits, cards, loans, and applications through stable, versioned APIs, webhooks, and event streams. Oradian is independently audited to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 and aligns to CBN, BSP, and OJK regulatory requirements.

companies.name: Morado
companies.description: Morado is a Colombian fintech and B2B marketplace for the beauty and wellness industry across Latin America, founded in 2022 by Angela Maria Acosta (an early Rappi employee). It is the "everything store for beauty shops" — giving salons, spas, and independent beauty entrepreneurs (a workforce that is majority women) access to intelligent credit, working-capital lines, inventory supply, inventory management, last-mile logistics, and digital tools through a 100% digital process, even for businesses without a traditional financial history. Credit applications run over WhatsApp with 30/60/90-day revolving lines and 3-12 month term products, serving 32,000+ micro-business clients. Backed by QED Investors, Andreessen Horowitz, Tiger Global, H20 Capital, Latitud, and Village Global. Public surface is the moradocolombia.com marketing/credit site (built on Wix) — no first-party developer API, though the Wix site exposes a hosted MCP endpoint and an llms.txt.

companies.name: Plink
companies.description: Plink is a personalized commerce and card-linking platform that turns everyday payment transactions into intelligent, permission-based savings and engagement experiences for banks, merchants, and consumers. Its technology enriches transactions in real time, applying business rules and automated actions across payments, digital banking, and customer engagement, and exposes an API that lets any payment network make its transactions "smart" while keeping consumers anonymous. Plink says it has personalized over 700 million transactions and reaches 350+ banks, hundreds of thousands of merchants, and 10+ million consumers through an invitation-only network. The company operates a merchant/business portal and a consumer savings program (Fancoins) built on a PCI-compliant, tokenized card-linking structure.

companies.name: Raymond James Bank
companies.description: Raymond James Bank is a Florida-chartered state member bank headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Raymond James Financial, Inc. (NYSE: RJF), a diversified financial services holding company founded in 1962. Supervised by the Federal Reserve and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, the bank provides securities-based lending, residential mortgages, commercial and industrial and commercial real estate loans, tax-exempt loans, and deposit products (including its Enhanced Savings Program) primarily to Raymond James wealth-management and institutional clients. On open finance, the bank runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators such as Plaid. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented for this institution as of this record.

companies.name: Warblerlabs
companies.description: Warbler Labs is a San Francisco fintech and blockchain company (founded 2020 by Blake West and Michael Sall) that builds and contributes to the Goldfinch Protocol, a decentralized credit protocol for real-world asset lending that provides stablecoin loans and yield generated by off-chain economic activity, and UID (Unique Identity), a KYC/KYB-compliant on-chain identity NFT. The public developer surface is the Goldfinch smart-contract system on Ethereum, an open-source monorepo (github.com/goldfinch-eng), a hosted GraphQL subgraph that indexes protocol state, and developer documentation at dev.goldfinch.finance. Security is central: every release is audited by external firms (CertiK, Trail of Bits) and the protocol runs a $500k Immunefi bug bounty.

companies.name: Oatfi
companies.description: OatFi is a fintech infrastructure company that describes itself as "The Modern Credit Network for B2B Payments." It provides embedded credit, lending, and working-capital products that platforms and marketplaces can offer inside their own payment workflows. Its product surface spans Accounts Payable (flexible payment terms for buyers), Accounts Receivable (guaranteed or early supplier payouts), and Commercial Charge Cards (scaled credit and capital for commercial card programs), backed by modular components for KYB and fraud verification, underwriting, origination, loan management, capital-markets access, and collections. OatFi exposes these capabilities through APIs for approvals, settlements, and reconciliation. The developer documentation (docs.oatfi.com, a ReadMe hub) and dashboard are access-gated, so no public OpenAPI or API reference is available for cataloging at this time. Backed by QED Investors.

companies.name: One
companies.description: OnePay (formerly One / One Finance) is a Walmart-backed consumer fintech that delivers a single mobile app combining banking, high-yield savings, a CashRewards debit card, a credit-building card, buy-now-pay-later, investing, cryptocurrency trading, and tax filing. Banking services are provided through partner banks Coastal Community Bank and Lead Bank (Members FDIC). The product is consumer-facing with no public developer API; a partner/developer portal exists behind authentication at developer.onepay.com. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment.

companies.name: Avant
companies.description: Avant is a Chicago-based financial technology company that provides consumer credit products to middle-income U.S. consumers, primarily unsecured personal loans of roughly $2,000-$35,000 (9.95%-35.99% APR, 24-60 month terms) for debt consolidation, emergencies, home improvement, and other needs, alongside the Avant Credit Card issued through WebBank. Founded in 2012 and backed by investors including QED Investors and 500 Global, Avant operates a mobile-first lending and card-servicing platform with a customer help center, personal-finance blog, and SCRA support for military members. Avant is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer API or portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and support surfaces.

companies.name: Desjardins Group
companies.description: Desjardins Group (Mouvement Desjardins) is the largest cooperative financial group in North America, founded in 1900 in Lévis, Quebec by Alphonse Desjardins. It is a federation of caisses populaires (member-owned credit unions) rather than a share-capital chartered bank, comprising the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec and its subsidiaries, the caisses in Quebec and the Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union, regulated in Quebec by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). It holds roughly CAD $470 billion in assets and serves more than 7.8 million members and clients with personal, business, wealth-management and insurance products. On open finance, Desjardins publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification; developer.desjardins.com and other API-portal subdomains do not resolve, and consumer financial-data access is delivered today through third-party aggregators (Flinks, Plaid, Finicity, Tink) via screen-scraping/aggregator connectivity rather than a documented Desjardins API. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024/2025, overseen by the FCAC) but not yet operational; as a cooperative outside the Big Six, Desjardins may opt in to Phase 1 rather than being mandated.

companies.name: OakNorth
companies.description: OakNorth is a UK-based commercial bank and business-lending institution founded in 2015, providing debt financing to mid-market and lower-mid-market businesses in the UK and, through its New York team, the United States. Its products span business loans (from roughly GBP 1m to tens of millions), commercial real estate lending, commercial & industrial cash-flow financing, fund finance, and business and personal savings accounts. OakNorth is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It publicly exposes no developer API, open-banking API, or developer portal; its public technical surface is limited to a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program and standard web/legal properties. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Zone & Company
companies.description: Zone & Co (Zone & Company) is a NetSuite-native financial operations software vendor whose SuiteApp suite automates the back office across five product families - Quote to Cash (ZoneBilling billing and revenue recognition, ZonePayments Stripe integration), Procure to Pay (ZoneProcure, ZoneCapture, ZoneApprovals), Treasury (ZoneLiquidity cash forecasting, ZoneReconcile), Payroll Management (ZonePayroll, Employee Portal), and Record to Report (ZoneReporting on Power BI, Data Warehouse, ZoneExtract, Solution 7). The products are delivered as native Oracle NetSuite SuiteApps distributed through the SuiteApp Marketplace rather than as a standalone public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Alogent
companies.description: Alogent is a banking and financial technology provider that delivers cloud-native software to banks and credit unions across three product families: payments and deposit automation (Unify omni-channel check capture across branch, mobile, and ATM/ITM), intelligent check fraud detection and mitigation (Alogent Shield and Shield+), and enterprise content and loan document management (FASTdocs, AccuAccount, and the Alogent Document Portal). The platform emphasizes workflow automation, compliance controls, real-time transaction processing, and AI-assisted fraud prevention for financial institutions of all sizes. Alogent is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. No public developer portal or API documentation surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: AAZZUR
companies.description: AAZZUR is a Berlin-based embedded finance and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets enterprises, financial institutions, and startups embed financial services into their own products. It provides modular "Smart Finance Blocks" (pre-configured front-end screens, micro-services, and connections to underlying API providers) alongside its own developer-portal APIs and a smart marketplace of BaaS and fintech partners. Customers can consume the APIs directly, drop in AAZZUR's embeddable front-end components, or launch stand-alone apps and web frontends covering banking, payments, cards, lending, wealth management, and insurance without building the underlying financial infrastructure themselves.

companies.name: M2P Fintech
companies.description: M2P Fintech is Asia's largest API infrastructure company, powering banking, lending, and payment solutions for fintechs, banks, NBFCs, and enterprises. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Chennai, India, M2P operates across 30+ countries and processes 20+ billion transactions for 50+ million end customers. Its modular, cloud-native, API-first product suite lets businesses embed financial services — core banking (Turing CBS), card issuance (credit, debit, prepaid, forex), UPI, cross-border payments, loan origination and management (Finflux), merchant management, BNPL, microfinance, KYC (Syntizen), reconciliation (Recon360), fraud and AML monitoring, 3DS access control, and neobanking — with up to 5X faster go-to-market.

companies.name: Clearscore
companies.description: ClearScore is a London-founded fintech (2015) that gives consumers free access to their credit score and report and matches them to financial products — credit cards, loans, car finance, insurance and more — through a personalised financial marketplace. It also runs ClearScore Protect (dark-web identity monitoring), DriveScore (driving-behaviour scoring) and Open Banking features, and operates across the UK, South Africa, Australia, Canada and New Zealand. Its B2B arm, ClearScore Connect, exposes credit-data and eligibility services to partner lenders through a partner-gated developer portal (docs.clearscore.com). Backed by QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearScore's developer API is documented behind a password-gated ReadMe.io portal, so no public OpenAPI or machine-readable spec could be captured.

companies.name: First Horizon
companies.description: First Horizon Corporation is a Fortune 500 financial services holding company headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. Through First Horizon Bank it provides commercial, private, consumer, and mortgage banking, wealth management, and capital markets services across the southern United States. First Horizon operates a real API Banking developer portal for Treasury Management clients, exposing RESTful products for money movement, ACH origination, real-time account information, and routing-number lookups, secured with OAuth 2.0 and a sandbox for build-and-test integration. Onboarding is partner/relationship gated and no OpenAPI/Swagger specifications are publicly downloadable — this repository captures the documented API surface honestly, humanURL-only.

companies.name: LendingClub
companies.description: LendingClub is a US consumer-finance company and digital bank, originally founded in 2006 as a peer-to-peer marketplace lender and later a national bank holding company after its 2021 acquisition of Radius Bancorp. In 2026 the company rebranded as Happen Bank, N.A. (a wholly-owned subsidiary of Happen, Inc.) and moved its public web presence from lendingclub.com to happen.com, where it offers personal loans, auto refinancing, business loans, LevelUp checking and savings accounts, the DebtIQ credit dashboard, and an institutional investing program for marketplace-lending loan buyers. LendingClub historically published a public Investor API for its retail notes marketplace; that marketplace was retired in December 2020 and the developer portal and API documentation are no longer published. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no public developer program, API reference, or SDK surface, and no OpenAPI or event specifications are available to harvest.

companies.name: Mission Lane
companies.description: Mission Lane is a consumer fintech founded in 2018 that offers the Mission Lane Visa credit card (issued by WebBank) to help millions of Americans with limited or rebuilding credit gain access to transparent, fair credit. Operating as a remote-first company backed by QED Investors, it combines modern data science and machine-learning underwriting with the discipline of an established financial institution, and partners with Plaid for open-finance connectivity. Mission Lane provides a mobile app and a web account dashboard for cardholders but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or partner API program; its engineering surface (BentoML model services, MLOps tooling) is internal.

companies.name: Uni
companies.description: Uni (Uni Cards) is an Indian consumer credit fintech founded in 2020 by Nitin Gupta, Prateek Jindal, and Laxmikant Vyas that delivers clutter-breaking credit products to consumers in India, including pay-later style credit cards and flexible repayment products. Uni is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. The company is a consumer-facing app-first business and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API surface.

companies.name: Zibo
companies.description: Zibo (operating as Azibo) is a financial services and property-management platform for independent landlords and rental property owners. The company offers a free-to-use platform that bundles rent collection, tenant screening, online rental applications, lease agreements and eSignatures, document storage, maintenance and messaging, banking, and rental-property accounting. Azibo monetizes through interest on cash balances, card-transaction fees, paid lease/eSignature and screening products, and renter subscriptions such as credit-boost programs. The product is delivered as a SaaS web application (app.azibo.com) that integrates third-party providers including Stripe, Plaid, TransUnion, Latchel, and signNow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. Zibo was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

companies.name: Commerce Bank
companies.description: Commerce Bank is the principal banking subsidiary of Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ CBSH), a Missouri-based regional bank holding company with roughly $32 billion in assets and dual headquarters in Kansas City and St. Louis. Commerce Bank is a Missouri state-chartered bank and Federal Reserve member, founded in 1865, offering personal, business, commercial, and wealth-management services across the U.S. Midwest. Its API posture is corporate/embedded-banking oriented rather than a fully open public program: it runs a registration-gated external developer portal (developers.commercebank.com) and a CommercePayments developer platform, and delivers ERP-embedded banking via Commerce Connections Direct. Consumer-permissioned data sharing is largely intermediated through aggregators such as Plaid and platforms like Modern Treasury rather than a documented first-party, self-serve open-banking API. No public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is publicly available.

companies.name: Dave
companies.description: Dave is a U.S. consumer financial-technology company (Nasdaq: DAVE), founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that operates a mobile banking app serving roughly 14 million members. Its products include ExtraCash short-term cash advances of up to $500 (underwritten with its CashAI cash-flow model rather than credit scores), an FDIC-insured Dave Checking account with early direct deposit and Round-Up savings, and a Goals savings account. Banking services are provided through partner banks such as Coastal Community Bank. Dave is a consumer app and does not publish a first-party public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal: there is no developer.dave.com / docs.dave.com, and api.dave.com is the app's private, undocumented mobile backend. Programmatic access to Dave-held consumer data is aggregator-mediated — Dave both consumes Plaid (to let members link external accounts) and is reachable as a supported institution through open-finance aggregators. This profile captures its public identity, aggregator-only open-finance posture, commercial link surface, and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Klar
companies.description: Klar is a Mexican digital financial services platform (neobank) headquartered in Mexico City with engineering in Berlin, serving roughly 7 million customers. Regulated by Mexico's CNBV, Klar offers a deposit account with yield, a no-annual-fee credit card, a secured (garantizada) credit card, the metal Platino card, personal loans, investment products, and Chubb-underwritten life and fraud insurance, plus cashback and interest-free-months (MSI) benefits. It also runs Klar Empresarial for business customers, partnered with Uber to launch the Uber Card in Mexico, and announced the acquisition of mortgage fintech Yave. Klar's product surface is delivered entirely through its consumer mobile app and website; as of this profile Klar publishes NO public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or sandbox, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or webhook surface could be found. Third-party access to Klar accounts is generally brokered through Latin American open-finance aggregators (Belvo, Pluggy, Plaid) rather than a first-party Klar API. Klar does operate a public GitHub organization (klar-mx), but its repositories are internal infrastructure and DevOps tooling and forks, not client libraries for a Klar API.

companies.name: Trezy
companies.description: Trezy is a Franco-Dutch fintech SaaS (Trezy SAS, founded 2021 in Paris by Quentin Lacointa) offering AI-driven cash flow management for small and medium businesses across Europe, the US, and Canada. It connects to 2,000+ banks via PSD2/Open Banking to deliver real-time cash position, automatic AI transaction categorization, 95%-accurate 12-month cash flow forecasting, real-time P&L, 27+ financial KPIs, supplier cost analysis, and OCR-based document management from a single platform starting at a free tier. Trezy also offers dedicated plans for external CFOs (DAF) and accounting firms, and integrates with QuickBooks Online and Pennylane. Backed by Seedcamp and Playfair Capital (with Kima Ventures and Discovery Ventures) in a €3M seed round. Trezy publishes an llms.txt corpus and an /.well-known/ai-plugin.json manifest but does not expose a public developer API.

companies.name: Arq
companies.description: Arq (formerly DolarApp) is a Latin American cross-border fintech app that gives travelers, investors, and professionals digital dollar and digital euro accounts at real market rates without hidden fees. Founded in 2021, the mobile-first platform offers currency conversion, a borderless payment card, global accounts to send and receive international payments, bill payment, PIX transfers, stock and ETF investing, and high-yield Trade and Save accounts, plus ARQ Premium and Prestige tiers. Arq raised $70M from Sequoia Capital and Founders Fund and serves over 2 million users across the Americas. Arq is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: BECU
companies.description: BECU (Boeing Employees' Credit Union) is a member-owned, not-for-profit state-chartered credit union founded in 1935 and headquartered in Tukwila, Washington (NMLS ID 490518). Originally serving Boeing employees, it is today one of the largest credit unions in the United States, offering consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, and investment services across the Pacific Northwest and nationally through digital channels. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, BECU exposes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; its digital banking runs on established core and fintech vendors (FIS, LPL/Client Point, ICE/Ellie Mae for mortgage), and consumer-permissioned data access for third-party fintech apps is intermediated through data aggregators rather than a documented, self-serve BECU API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and no mandated open-banking API contract applies here; the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule is the emerging framework that will shape BECU's future data-access posture.

companies.name: Charlie Finance
companies.description: Charlie (Charlie Finance Co.) was a Pasadena, California fintech company that operated a mobile banking app and debit-card program built specifically for Americans aged 62 and older. Founded in 2021 by Kevin Nazemi, the service offered Social Security deposits paid up to several days early, a FraudShield protection layer tuned to scams that target seniors, 3% high-yield savings, no monthly fees or minimums, a fee-free Allpoint ATM network of 55,000+ machines, custom photo debit cards, and seven-day-a-week human customer support. Charlie is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and raised a $7.5M seed round followed by a $23M Series A. The company discontinued service and permanently closed its debit-card program on January 22, 2026. Charlie is a consumer neobank and does not publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: Comun
companies.description: Comun (Común) is a fintech company providing digital banking and money-transfer services designed for Latino immigrants in the United States. Through a bilingual (Spanish/English) mobile app, users open an FDIC-insured U.S. checking account with a valid national ID and no SSN required, get a Visa debit card, receive early direct deposit up to two days ahead of payday, and send international remittances to 17+ Latin American countries via the app or WhatsApp. Banking services are provided through Community Federal Savings Bank; remittance and P2P rails run on UniTeller and Cross River Bank. Comun is backed by Costanoa Ventures and Redpoint Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; Comun operates as a consumer neobank and does not publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Covalto
companies.description: Covalto (formerly Credijusto) is a Mexican digital bank for small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Mexico City. It offers business and personal checking accounts, fixed-rate investment products, quick working-capital credit (Agil Covalto), factoring, leasing (arrendamiento), and fiduciary trust services (fideicomisos). Covalto acquired a regulated Mexican banking license, making it one of the first fintechs in Mexico to become a fully licensed bank. Its digital surface spans online banking, digital account opening, and a credit application flow. Covalto is backed by QED Investors. As of the latest review it publishes no public API developer portal; its developer documentation at docs.covalto.com is gated behind Google Identity-Aware Proxy for internal use.

companies.name: Crosslend
companies.description: CrossLend is a Berlin-based fintech providing digital debt technology for the private lending and securitisation space. Its platform offers Portfolio Analytics for loan-level data validation, granular portfolio insights and automated reporting, and Securitisation-as-a-Service that digitises and automates the issuance of financial instruments, including SPV setup, legal and compliance frameworks and audit-proof reporting. CrossLend serves banks, asset managers and institutional lenders across Europe, and is backed by Earlybird and Northzone. The company exposes no public developer API surface today; this profile tracks its identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Endl
companies.description: Endl is a financial-technology company offering "the operating account for borderless businesses." The platform lets consulting firms, agencies, contractors, marketplaces, and importers/exporters collect payments in 9+ currencies, send to 160+ countries, hold balances in USD, EUR, GBP and regulated stablecoins, and spend through physical and virtual Visa corporate cards with spend controls — all from a single dashboard. Endl positions itself against Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Deel, Mercury and Airwallex, and is backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface is currently advertised; the product is dashboard-first.

companies.name: First Hawaiian Bank
companies.description: First Hawaiian Bank is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution, founded in 1858 and headquartered at First Hawaiian Center in Honolulu. It is a Hawaii state-chartered commercial bank and member FDIC, operating as the principal subsidiary of First Hawaiian, Inc. (NASDAQ ticker FHB), a publicly traded bank holding company. The bank serves consumer and commercial customers through roughly 57 branches in Hawaii plus locations in Guam and Saipan, offering deposit accounts, lending, wealth management, treasury/cash management, and merchant services. On the open-finance front, First Hawaiian operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer.fhb.com, api.fhb.com, and fhb.com/en/developers returned no host or HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a direct bank API. No documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found as of this record. Its commercial online banking product (FHB Commercial Online, formerly OBC) is a traditional web application rather than a developer-facing API surface.

companies.name: Get
companies.description: Get (useget.com) is a Singapore-based fintech company offering a mobile banking and financial-literacy platform for children, teens, and their families. The Get app pairs separate kid and parent accounts with prepaid Visa cards, parental spending controls, automated weekly allowances, a chore-based reward system, real-time spending analytics, and savings-goal folders, so young people can practice using real money tools in a safe, supervised environment. Get sells consumer subscription tiers (Get Core and Get Plus) plus a family account, and operates under a Payment Services exemption in Singapore. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification is published at this time; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Goin
companies.description: Goin is a European consumer fintech platform, backed by Anthemis and based in Barcelona, Spain, that helps more than 700,000 users across Europe grow their money and spend less. The app bundles automated savings (fixed daily, weekly or monthly rules and goal-based portfolios), investing, buying and selling of cryptocurrencies, cashback and rewards at hundreds of online and physical stores, gift cards and coupons, and a browser extension that surfaces discounts while shopping. Bank accounts are connected securely under Europe's PSD2 open banking regulation, and a referral program rewards users for inviting friends. Goin is a business-to-consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer program, API, or documentation surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks Goin as a portfolio lead and captures its public web, help, and legal presence.

companies.name: Highbeam
companies.description: Highbeam is a business banking and finance platform built for modern consumer brands (direct-to-consumer and e-commerce). It brings together operating and high-yield accounts, a charge card that pays cashback on advertising spend, working capital and credit lines, automated bill pay, and spend intelligence, alongside Luma, an applied-AI finance assistant. Banking services are delivered through partner banks (Thread Bank, member FDIC) and Airwallex. Highbeam is based in New York City. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this entry captures the company identity, its public web properties, and a live domain-security probe.

companies.name: MeridianLink
companies.description: MeridianLink provides a powerful web service enabling software applications to retrieve consumer credit data in XML format. It offers lending and credit platform solutions for financial institutions.

companies.name: Nave Bank
companies.description: Nave Bank is a digital-first business bank based in Puerto Rico, offering FDIC-insured deposit accounts, business savings, and business loans through an easy-to-navigate online and mobile banking platform. Its product surface centers on business checking ("Cuenta Nave Business"), interest-bearing savings, real-time payments, ACH and wire transfers, and mobile check deposit, with a bilingual (Spanish/English) experience and human customer support. Nave was surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Nave Bank publishes a consumer/business banking website and help center but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

companies.name: Onecard
companies.description: OneCard is a mobile-first metal credit card from India's FPL Technologies, a fintech unicorn that reimagines credit and payments with full-stack, in-house technology. OneCard is issued in partnership with banks including Bank of Baroda, CSB Bank, Federal Bank, SBM Bank, South Indian Bank and Indian Bank, and emphasizes simplicity, transparency and giving control back to the user. FPL Technologies also operates OneScore (credit-score monitoring) and Wizely (savings). Backed by QED Investors, OneCard is a consumer-facing product; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Provide
companies.description: Provide is a financial services division of Fifth Third Bank offering banking and financing built specifically for owners of professional practices — dental, medical, veterinary, optometry, childcare, financial advisory, funeral, and insurance businesses. The company provides conventional and SBA loans to start, acquire, or expand a practice, alongside a full suite of customized banking products. Provide was acquired by Fifth Third Bank and operates as a specialty lending and banking brand. Surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Tangerine
companies.description: Tangerine is a Canadian direct (branchless) bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a federally regulated Schedule I bank chartered as Tangerine Bank (institution number 614). Founded in 1997 as ING Direct Canada, it was acquired by Scotiabank in 2012 and rebranded as Tangerine in 2014; it remains a separate legal entity operating as Scotiabank's digital-banking arm, serving roughly two million clients with no-fee chequing and savings accounts, GICs, mortgages, mutual funds, and a cash-back Mastercard delivered entirely through mobile and web. On API and open-finance posture, Tangerine publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; Canada has no operational consumer-driven-banking mandate yet (the federal framework is legislated but not live), so third-party access to Tangerine account and transaction data today is aggregator-based via Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard) rather than through a documented first-party API.

companies.name: Deduce
companies.description: Deduce is a New York City-based identity intelligence and fraud-prevention company focused on detecting stolen and synthetic identities, including the rapidly growing class of AI-generated identities used to bypass traditional Know Your Customer and onboarding controls. The company operates the Deduce Identity Graph, an activity-backed U.S. identity network the firm describes as covering 185 million weekly active users and 1.5 billion daily events, used to deliver real-time multi-contextual risk and fraud signals during new account opening, login, and checkout. Deduce sells a real-time API-based fraud-risk scoring product, a Multicontextual Identity Insights service, and a browser-based dashboard for traffic segmentation, anomaly detection, and forensic review, with pre-built integrations into common identity platforms (Auth0, Microsoft Entra External ID / Azure AD B2C, ForgeRock / Ping, Gluu) alongside a native REST API. The company sells to banks, fintechs, lenders, BNPL providers, retail, travel, and payments platforms; its commercial model is enterprise contracts, and its developer documentation, OpenAPI definitions, and integration guides sit behind an authenticated portal, with no public GitHub repositories, no public SDKs, and no published machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: MANTL
companies.description: MANTL is an account and deposit origination software company for banks and credit unions. Its omnichannel platform lets financial institutions open consumer and business deposit and loan accounts across online and in-branch channels, integrating with existing core banking systems to modernize onboarding and accelerate deposit growth. More than 100 institutions raise over $1 billion in deposits monthly through the platform. MANTL was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public API or developer portal — this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and system-status surfaces.

companies.name: IndusInd Bank
companies.description: IndusInd Bank Limited is a new-generation Indian private-sector bank, established in April 1994 and headquartered in Mumbai, offering commercial, retail, and electronic banking across accounts, deposits, cards, loans, investments, and insurance for personal, NRI, business, and corporate customers. The bank operates a public developer portal at sandbox.indusind.com that publishes REST APIs for core banking, cards, deposits, and account services (for example Finacle FD Servicing, DCMS Card Inquiry on CIF, CBS Enquiry, Digital Account Balance Inquiry, and debit transaction APIs), each with an interactive Try console after registration. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched with its real developer surface.

companies.name: Traive
companies.description: Traive is a Brazilian agri-fintech that connects agribusiness with financial investors, using AI and data analytics to simplify credit access in the agricultural sector. Its Traive Agro product handles agricultural credit commercialization with risk analysis, process automation, and financing access, while Traive Finance provides credit risk analysis and access to qualified agricultural assets with traceability. The platform serves 160K+ registered producers and manages over R$6B in structured recurring credit operations. Traive publishes no public developer API; its platform authenticates via a Keycloak OpenID Connect provider whose public discovery documents reveal an internal service estate (credit, farmers, retailers, ERP integration, GraphQL) captured in this profile.

companies.name: Cadence Bank
companies.description: Cadence Bank is a regional U.S. commercial bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi and Houston, Texas, formed in October 2021 when legacy Cadence Bancorporation merged into BancorpSouth Bank (the surviving entity, subsequently renamed Cadence Bank; NYSE ticker CADE). It is a Mississippi state-chartered bank operating roughly 400+ branches across the U.S. South, Midwest, and Texas with about $48-50 billion in assets, offering consumer banking, mortgages, home equity, credit cards, small business and commercial banking, treasury management, and wealth/insurance services. On open finance, Cadence Bank exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), which is the honest, prevailing posture for most U.S. regional banks. No documented direct FDX (Financial Data Exchange) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access API was found as of this profile.

companies.name: Fincompare
companies.description: Fincompare (now operating under the Fynbiz brand alongside Compeon) is a Berlin-based digital financing marketplace for small and medium-sized enterprises. Founded in 2017, the platform lets businesses request, compare, and close financing offers from 100+ banks and alternative lenders in one place, covering business loans, leasing, factoring, goods and warehouse financing, real-estate financing, and revenue-based financing. Fincompare connects lenders such as ING, VR Smart Finanz, and iwoca directly through bank API integrations to automate credit decisions. The company was acquired by a consortium of DZ Bank, several Volksbanken, and Atruvia in 2021. Fincompare operates a customer-facing SME financing product; it does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

companies.name: Noh
companies.description: Noh is a Brazilian consumer fintech (neobank) founded in November 2021 by Ana Zucato and Octavio Turra, headquartered in Sao Paulo, SP. Noh pioneered Brazil's first joint account and shared card for couples, letting two partners manage money together with equal permissions, real-time expense visibility, automatic categorization, and a shared spending limit based on combined income. Products include a joint checking account, a shared Visa card (prepaid and credit), and payments via Pix, boleto, and card, plus joint investing. It is a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) with no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time. Backed by Kindred Ventures and other investors; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile.

companies.name: Palm
companies.description: Palm is an AI cash flow forecasting platform for corporate treasury and finance teams. It sits above existing Treasury Management Systems (TMS) and ERPs, unifying visibility across cash positions and forecasting liquidity directly from bank and transaction data. Palm learns the timing and size of recurring cash flows from historical transactions to keep a rolling 13-week-and-longer forecast current automatically, and combines ERP data, bank transactions, and 25+ AI models to improve forecast accuracy by over 60%. The product spans AI cash forecasting, what-if scenario modeling, continuous forecast-vs-actual variance analysis, automated daily cash positioning across banks and currencies, surplus-cash investment identification, board-ready treasury reporting, and a "Pulse" anomaly-detection assistant. Palm is a speedinvest portfolio company. It integrates with TMS (Coupa, FIS, ION, Kyriba), banks (Citi, HSBC, J.P. Morgan), investment platforms, data warehouses, and ERPs (SAP, IFS), but does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: PrecisionLender
companies.description: PrecisionLender is a relationship pricing and profitability platform for commercial banks, now part of Q2 Holdings (acquired 2019). It equips relationship managers, treasury officers, and credit teams to price and structure optimal commercial deals with total relationship visibility, in-deal collaboration, and "Andi", an AI coaching engine that surfaces in-the-moment pricing guidance. The product draws market-competitive intelligence from 150+ financial institutions and integrates into a bank's technology stack to reduce manual data entry. The standalone precisionlender.com site now redirects to the Q2 "Relationship Pricing and Profitability" product; there is no independent public PrecisionLender API, and Q2's developer surface (Q2 Innovation Studio) requires authentication.

companies.name: Slice
companies.description: Slice is an Indian consumer fintech and small finance bank, founded in 2016 as SlicePay by Rajan Bajaj and headquartered between Bengaluru (corporate) and Guwahati (registered). The company originally built a buy-now-pay-later product and a prepaid-card-plus-credit-line offering aimed at students and young professionals — pitched as a credit-card alternative for India's Gen Z — and at its peak was reportedly issuing over 300,000 prepaid cards per month before RBI's 2022 restrictions on credit-linked PPI products forced a pivot. In October 2023 Slice announced a merger with the regulated North East Small Finance Bank (NESFB), the first fintech-into-bank merger in India; the merger received RBI approval in October 2023, CCI approval in March 2024 and NCLT (Guwahati) approval in August 2024, completed on October 27, 2024, and the combined entity was rebranded as Slice Small Finance Bank in May 2025. Today Slice operates a consumer mobile-first neobank — savings accounts, fixed deposits, UPI, a Slice credit card and rewards — alongside a merchant-facing payments stack exposed through a Merchant API (api.nebank.com) covering bank-account validation, payouts, pay-in/collect, refunds, virtual accounts, balance, transactions and webhook notifications. As of late 2024 the company had raised approximately $387M from investors including Tiger Global, Insight Partners and Blume Ventures.

companies.name: CIT Group
companies.description: CIT Group was a US financial holding company providing commercial financing, equipment leasing, factoring, and middle-market banking services. CIT was acquired by First Citizens BancShares in January 2022 and has been integrated into First Citizens Bank as the Commercial Banking division. CIT Group does not maintain a public developer portal and never published general-purpose REST APIs; legacy customer integrations were delivered through file-based ACH/wire feeds, the OneWest online banking platform, and partner-mediated treasury connectivity. New API-based integrations for the combined institution are now exposed through First Citizens Bank.

companies.name: Heartland Financial USA
companies.description: Heartland Financial USA is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Heartland Financial USA API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: JPMorgan Chase
