The system is designed to align with SR 11-7 and OCC guidance on AI governance and third-party risk, and claims to compress underwriting from weeks to minutes while enabling loan closures in under ten days. Proximitty publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; it is delivered as a hosted SaaS product, and its public surface is limited to a marketing site, blog, security/compliance page, and a hosted Trust Center.

companies.name: Regular Finance
companies.description: Regular Finance (Regular) is a French fintech offering a consumer digital-asset yield account. Customers deposit euros by bank transfer and earn roughly 5.50% annual interest paid daily, backed by regulated stablecoins such as EURC and USDC placed into on-chain liquidity pools and yield protocols. Withdrawals are free at any time and no crypto knowledge is required. Regular is a Techstars-backed company headquartered in France; the product is entirely consumer-facing (web and mobile app at app.regular.eu) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or technical documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: SarisAI
companies.description: SarisAI (Saris) builds agentic AI workflow automation for banks and credit unions, automating multi-step back-office operations across lending, compliance, and operations while keeping human oversight and audit trails. Its platform runs six specialized AI agents (Document, System, Inbox, Audit & Monitoring, External, and Income & Financial Analysis) that handle document intake, income verification, data validation, borrower communication, and post-close regulatory checks across mortgage, consumer, and commercial lending. Saris integrates directly with core banking, loan origination, and document systems (Fiserv, Encompass, OnBase/Hyland, Meridian) and LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini). The company is a Homebrew-backed fintech and is SOC 2, GDPR, GLBA, and CUSO certified. It is a private B2B platform with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or self-service surface; this profile captures its identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sidekick
companies.description: Sidekick is a UK-based online wealth management and investing platform that offers expert-led investments and savings products once reserved for the ultra-wealthy, delivered through a mobile app and web platform. Its product range spans managed investment portfolios, savings accounts, private equity access, and cryptocurrency exposure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp, Sidekick is a consumer (B2C) fintech and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: UBS Bank USA
companies.description: UBS Bank USA (BUSA) is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank and FDIC-insured depository institution headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, established in 2003 and reporting roughly $122 billion in total assets. It is the primary US banking vehicle of UBS Wealth Management Americas, providing FDIC-insured deposit sweep programs, securities-based lending, mortgages, and credit cards almost exclusively to the high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth advisory clients of parent UBS Group AG. It is supervised by the FDIC, the Utah Department of Financial Institutions, and the CFPB. Unlike a fintech or a Banking-as-a-Service provider, UBS Bank USA exposes no first-party public developer API surface of its own; its services are delivered through UBS Financial Advisors rather than self-serve APIs. The only live UBS developer portal (developer.ubs.com) belongs to UBS Switzerland and serves Swiss and EU products (key4 mortgages, QR-bill, PSD2, TWINT, bLink, KeyPort/EBICS), not this US entity. US consumer-permissioned data access, where available, is mediated by third-party aggregators rather than a documented BUSA API.

companies.name: Sallie Mae Bank
companies.description: Sallie Mae Bank is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank (industrial loan company) founded on November 28, 2005 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operating as the FDIC-insured banking subsidiary (FDIC cert #58177) of SLM Corporation (NASDAQ SLM), the publicly traded, S&P 400 consumer-finance company best known as the largest originator of private student loans in the United States. Beyond student and education lending, the bank offers retail deposit products including high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit through salliemae.com. Sallie Mae Bank does not operate a first-party public developer program - there is no developer.salliemae.com portal, no api.salliemae.com host, and no published OpenAPI/Swagger definitions. Consumer account and transaction data is reachable only on a permissioned basis through third-party data aggregators (historically Plaid), and no first-party FDX data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture could be confirmed. This is an identity-only, aggregator-access record reflecting the honest reality that this institution exposes no public API surface.

companies.name: Live Oak Bank
companies.description: Live Oak Bank (Live Oak Banking Company) is a digital, branchless, North Carolina state-chartered commercial bank founded in 2008 and headquartered in Wilmington, NC, operating as the primary subsidiary of Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: LOB). It is the largest originator of U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) 7(a) loans in the country and serves small businesses in all 50 states with SBA and commercial lending, high-yield business and personal savings, CDs, and business checking with treasury services. Technology-forward for a bank of its size, Live Oak runs a cloud-native Finxact core (now Fiserv) with an Apiture-based digital banking platform, and in 2024 launched an in-house embedded-banking / Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) program that lets software companies deliver Live Oak deposit and payment products to their own customers. Its API surface is real but partner-gated: a production AWS API gateway operates at api.liveoak.bank (returning MissingAuthenticationToken to unauthenticated callers, with Live-Oak-specific lob-identity-id / lob-foreign-entity-id headers), but Live Oak publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no public API reference. Consumer-permissioned data access is available through account aggregators rather than a first-party public API, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented.

companies.name: Upswing
companies.description: Upswing Financial Technologies is an Indian open finance-as-a-service platform headquartered in Bengaluru and Mumbai. Its full-stack API platform lets consumer companies embed financial products such as deposits and lending from regulated partner banks (AU Small Finance Bank, DCB Bank, Utkarsh, Shivalik, Unity, South Indian Bank, Suryoday), while Upswing manages the bank integrations and compliance. Backed by QED Investors and Quona Capital. Upswing publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; its APIs are offered to partners under commercial agreements.

companies.name: Amex Bank of Canada
companies.description: Amex Bank of Canada is the Canadian banking subsidiary of the American Express Company (United States), incorporated in 1990 and headquartered in the Toronto area (Markham, Ontario). It is a Schedule II bank under Canada's Bank Act — a foreign-bank subsidiary regulated by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and treated as a Category II small-and-medium-sized deposit-taking institution — and it issues American Express charge and credit cards to Canadian consumers and businesses. As a card-centric Schedule II bank, Amex Bank of Canada runs no first-party developer portal of its own; the global American Express developer platform at developer.americanexpress.com is operated by the U.S. parent (a separate profile), not by this Canadian entity. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer, is not yet operational, so consumer data access to Amex-Canada accounts today is voluntary and largely aggregator-based rather than served by a public first-party API. This is an identity/provider record; no public Canadian API surface is documented.

companies.name: B2B Bank
companies.description: B2B Bank is a Schedule I Canadian bank, headquartered in Toronto and wholly owned by Laurentian Bank of Canada (Laurentian Bank Financial Group). It operates a business-to-business, intermediary-only model: rather than serving retail consumers directly, it manufactures and distributes banking products through a network of roughly 27,000 financial professionals — financial advisors and their dealerships, deposit and mortgage brokers and their firms, mutual fund and insurance manufacturers, and CIRO (formerly MFDA/IIROC) members. Its product lines include investment loans, RSP and TFSA loans, broker deposits (GICs and high-interest savings/investment accounts), broker mortgages, and investment and banking accounts. The bank became a Schedule I bank and adopted the B2B Bank name in 2012, consolidating predecessor trust businesses (North American Trust, Sun Life Trust), and its deposits are CDIC insured. On open finance, B2B Bank publishes no first-party developer portal or public API: developer.b2bbank.com and api.b2bbank.com do not resolve, and the public site exposes only gated advisor/broker applications (Advisor Access, EASE online loans, Group Access, Investor Access, online banking). Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, and the bank documents no FDX participation, Interac data-sharing API, or aggregator program of its own — consistent with an intermediary bank whose digital surface is partner-gated rather than developer-facing.

companies.name: Bankiom
companies.description: Bankiom is a Dubai-based consumer fintech founded in 2018 by Danny Abla. It began as a UAE/GCC lifestyle neobank offering free virtual prepaid Mastercard cards, multi-bank account aggregation, spending insights, and instant peer transfers through a mobile app across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman. Bankiom has since repositioned as an autonomous AI money agent that securely connects to a user's bank, audits roughly 90 days of transactions, and surfaces the fees, interest, unused rewards, forgotten subscriptions, and expiring loyalty points a customer should not be paying, charging only a capped share of verified savings. It is a consumer-facing application and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: CIBC Bank USA
companies.description: CIBC Bank USA is an Illinois state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #33306) headquartered at 120 South LaSalle Street in Chicago, Illinois. Formerly The PrivateBank and Trust Company, it was acquired in 2017 and rebranded, and today operates as a wholly owned US subsidiary of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) through the intermediate holding company CIBC Bancorp USA Inc. The bank focuses on commercial banking, capital markets, wealth management, trust services, private banking, and cross-border services for clients with North American operations, rather than mass-market retail. As a US regional institution, CIBC Bank USA publishes no first-party public developer portal or open API program; consumer-permissioned account and balance data is reached only through third-party aggregators such as Plaid, and the CIBC group has a data-access agreement with MX. It is not a documented direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participant and has published no explicit CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture, making its honest API surface aggregator-mediated only.

companies.name: Close Brothers
companies.description: Close Brothers Group plc (LSE: CBG) is a UK merchant banking group founded in 1878 and a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index, headquartered at 10 Crown Place, London EC2A 4FT. The group provides specialist lending across motor, premium, asset, invoice, and property finance; takes personal and business deposits through Close Brothers Savings; manages wealth through Close Brothers Asset Management; and trades securities through Winterflood. Its banking entity, Close Brothers Limited, is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA. Close Brothers is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks; it offers savings and deposit products rather than online payment (current) accounts, and therefore carries no UK Open Banking (OBIE / PSD2) Read/Write or Open Data publishing obligation. As of this profile no public developer portal, Open Banking Open Data endpoint, or documented API surface could be confirmed for the group.

companies.name: Finbots.AI
companies.description: Finbots.AI (finbots.ai) is a Singapore-headquartered fintech offering CreditX, a no-code, AI-powered credit risk platform that lets banks and lenders build, validate, and deploy application, behavioural, and collection scorecards in hours instead of months. Its proprietary, explainable machine-learning models power real-time lending decisions in under 0.03 seconds, and the platform adds a Decision Engine (business rules), propensity modelling, and managed data services. Backed by Accel, finbots.ai serves retail banking, SME lending, and credit-card clients across APAC and MEA markets, and was among the first fintechs to complete Singapore's AI Verify AI-governance testing framework. No public self-service developer API is published; API integration is enterprise and sales-gated.

companies.name: Meridian Credit Union
companies.description: Meridian Credit Union is Ontario's largest credit union and one of the largest in Canada — a member-owned financial cooperative headquartered in St. Catharines and Toronto, serving more than 365,000 members with roughly CAD $31 billion in assets under management, over 2,200 employees, and more than 75 years of history. Formed in 2005 through the merger of Niagara Credit Union and HEPCOE Credit Union, Meridian offers personal, business, and wealth banking and owns Meridian OneCap Credit Corp. (commercial equipment leasing and financing); it previously operated the federally chartered digital bank motusbank, which was wound down in 2023. As a provincially regulated Ontario credit union — overseen by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), with member deposits insured under Ontario's credit-union deposit-insurance scheme — Meridian is a cooperative, not a Schedule I or Schedule II bank. It publishes no first-party public developer API and no downloadable OpenAPI specification. Consumer-permissioned account-data access today is aggregator-mediated rather than first-party: Plaid maintains a Meridian institution connector, and the Central 1 / Flinks Outbound seam provides API-based data sharing for member credit unions. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in 2024 with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada / FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so Meridian's open-finance participation remains voluntary and aggregator-based.

companies.name: Modak
companies.description: Modak (Modak Makers) is a US consumer fintech that offers a family money-management app built around a free Visa debit card for kids and teens. Parents can assign chores and automate allowance, set savings goals with reward boosts, and use co-parenting tools, gift links, ATM access, bill splitting, and spending controls such as instant alerts, card freeze, and biometric security. Kids earn MBX reward points through daily steps and challenges that convert to pocket money, so they learn to spend, save, and manage money in real life. Modak is delivered as a mobile consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by GGV Capital.

companies.name: OneConnect
companies.description: OneConnect Financial Technology (NYSE: OCFT; HKEX: 6638) is a technology-as-a-service platform for financial institutions, incorporated in 2015 as an associate of China's Ping An Group to externalize its banking and insurance technology. Its cloud-native, microservices platform spans digital banking, digital insurance, and the Gamma platform (AI voice, computer vision, blockchain and big-data analytics), serving hundreds of banks and insurers across China and Southeast Asia with ready-to-integrate financial technology components exposed through Open APIs. OneConnect raised a US$650M Series A in 2018 from investors including the SoftBank Vision Fund and SBI Group. Its APIs are delivered as enterprise B2B integrations rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: Popular (Banco Popular)
companies.description: Popular, Inc. (NASDAQ: BPOP), operating as Banco Popular, is a publicly traded financial holding company founded in 1893 and headquartered in Hato Rey, San Juan, Puerto Rico. It is the largest bank in Puerto Rico and operates through two chartered depository segments: Banco Popular de Puerto Rico (BPPR), serving Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Popular Bank (formerly Banco Popular North America), a New York state-chartered commercial bank serving mainland U.S. markets including New York, New Jersey, and Florida. Popular is FDIC-insured and regulated as a U.S. bank holding company. On its open-finance and API posture, Popular does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications for its U.S. institutions (popular.com); consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available indirectly through third-party data aggregators such as Plaid, Tink, and Finicity rather than a direct bank API. This identity record reflects that honest reality — an aggregator-only access model with no documented first-party API surface, FDX membership, or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access program. (Note: the separate apiportal.popularenlinea.com open-banking portal belongs to Banco Popular Dominicano / Grupo Popular, a distinct Dominican Republic company, not to Popular, Inc.)

companies.name: Prosperity Bank
companies.description: Prosperity Bank is a Texas-chartered commercial bank (member FDIC, NMLS ID 466414) and the banking subsidiary of Prosperity Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: PB), a Houston, Texas based regional financial holding company with roughly $37-43 billion in total assets and 300-plus full-service branches across Texas and central Oklahoma. It offers consumer and commercial banking, treasury management, mortgage, and wealth services, and has grown largely through acquisitions (LegacyTexas, Lone Star State Bancshares, American Bank Holding, Southwest Bancshares, Stellar Bancorp). On open finance, Prosperity Bank operates no first-party public developer portal or documented API: developer. and api. subdomains do not resolve, and no /developers or /api pages exist. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (Finicity/Mastercard Open Banking, Plaid, and similar), not a directly published bank API. No FDX-conformant data-access API or CFPB Section 1033 posture is publicly documented by the bank as of this review.

companies.name: Santander US
companies.description: Santander Bank, N.A. (santanderbank.com) is the US retail and commercial banking subsidiary of Spain's Banco Santander S.A., headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It is a nationally chartered bank (National Association, regulated by the OCC) operating a branch network across the Northeast US (Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Delaware), which positions it as a super-regional bank. Unlike UK and Australian institutions bound by mandated open-banking contracts, and unlike US banks such as Capital One or Chase that publish first-party developer portals, Santander Bank N.A. exposes no public, first-party developer API for its US retail franchise: developer.santanderbank.com does not resolve, and the site publishes no developers/API/open-banking pages. Consumer-permissioned data access in the US is available today through aggregators rather than a direct API — Plaid supports "Santander - Personal" (Assets, Auth, Balance and Transactions). Santander's UK developer portal (developer.santander.co.uk) and the group's Corporate & Investment Banking API marketplace (apimarket.santandercib.com) are operated by separate legal entities and are not the US retail bank's surface. This record is an honest identity profile of a super-regional bank whose US open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated, with no documented first-party developer program.

companies.name: Security Service Federal Credit Union
companies.description: Security Service Federal Credit Union (SSFCU), headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative federally chartered and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving members across Texas, Colorado, and Utah with consumer and business banking, deposit accounts, credit cards, auto and mortgage lending, and investment services through branches, online banking, and mobile apps. Its open-finance posture is the norm for a US credit union: there is no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification, and no public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators, and any API capability is delivered through its core banking provider rather than a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: SouthState Bank
companies.description: SouthState Bank, National Association is an OCC-chartered national commercial bank headquartered in Winter Haven, Florida, and the principal subsidiary of SouthState Bank Corporation (NASDAQ: SSB). Formed through the 2020 merger of South State Corporation and CenterState Bank and redomiciled to Florida in 2025, it holds roughly $67 billion in assets and operates across the Southeast, Texas, Colorado, and Virginia. Like most US regional banks, SouthState runs no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definitions. Consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators rather than a direct API: the Open Banking Tracker records SouthState reachable via Plaid only, with no documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) endpoint and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access surface. Its open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, not a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Xalts
companies.description: Xalts (operated by Tokuten Pte Ltd) is an Accel-backed fintech building an AI agent platform for corporate treasury and finance teams — a copilot that automates trade finance operations (guarantees, trade payments, documentary credit and collections), liquidity management, and revenue operations. Task-specific agents learn internal processes and policies and integrate with ERPs, accounting systems, payment processors, and banks through the company's Omni Connect Protocol, which provides multi-bank connectivity via a single API. Xalts does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation; its connectivity APIs are offered to enterprise customers.

companies.name: BillTrim
companies.description: BillTrim is a consumer bill-management and negotiation service that helps households lower, monitor, and pay their recurring bills. Its team negotiates with providers on the customer's behalf (up to twice a year), watches for price increases before autopay processes, and can pay bills automatically from a connected bank account. BillTrim advertises support for 20,000+ service providers across internet, cable, phone, insurance, and other recurring household expenses. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API or developer portal is currently published.

companies.name: Carbon Direct
companies.description: Carbon Direct is a science-first carbon management company that pairs an enterprise carbon management platform with a team of 70+ scientists. The platform helps organizations measure emissions, set science-based targets, reduce, and procure high-quality carbon dioxide removal (CDR), with monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) capabilities expanded through its 2025 acquisition of Pachama. Carbon Direct is an enterprise SaaS and advisory offering and does not publish a public developer API as of this profile.

companies.name: PenFed Credit Union
companies.description: PenFed Credit Union (Pentagon Federal Credit Union), founded in 1935 and headquartered in McLean, Virginia, is a federally chartered credit union regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) and one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly 2.9 million members and tens of billions of dollars in assets. It is a not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperative that originally served the U.S. military and defense community and now offers open membership, providing mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, personal loans, and deposit accounts. On the open-finance front, PenFed runs an internal API-management practice — MuleSoft/Anypoint is the backbone of its digital-banking platform and an Apigee-backed developer portal host exists at developer.penfed.org (with an api.penfed.org gateway) — but neither surface is publicly documented or openly reachable: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and consumer account data is made available to members through permissioned third-party aggregators such as Plaid rather than a directly documented FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API.

companies.name: Tellus
companies.description: Tellus is a consumer fintech company whose mobile app pairs high-yield savings tools with real-estate-backed lending and property management. Members earn competitive rates on cash held in Tellus accounts, funded by the company's portfolio of residential real-estate loans, with deposits held at FDIC-insured partner banks. The app also offers a mobile wallet, a business wallet, and property-management tooling for landlords and property owners. Tellus is a private, venture-backed startup (an a16z portfolio company); it operates as a direct-to-consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

companies.name: Plum
companies.description: Plum is a UK-based personal finance "money app" that helps consumers save and invest automatically. Its mobile app pairs automated savings algorithms (eight saving automations) with a range of regulated products including Easy Access Savings, a Cash ISA, a 95-day Notice Account, a money-market Interest pocket, a Stocks & Shares ISA, a Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP), and access to thousands of stocks and funds. Plum operates under FCA oversight through multiple entities covering payment services, e-money, investment broking, and account information services, and monetizes via subscription tiers (Basic, Plus, Boost, Max). It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: @Stake
companies.description: Stake (Stake Technologies, Inc., NMLS #2535498) operates the "Return on Rent" cash-back network for renters. Renters earn cash back on their rent payments, build credit history through on-time payments, unlock exclusive local deals, and access banking services including an FDIC-insured checking account and debit card provided through banking partner Midland States Bank. Co-founded by Rowland Hobbs and Jimmy Jacobson, the platform reports more than 550,000 homes in its network and over $50M in cash back earned by renters, averaging roughly $350 per renter annually. Stake is a consumer-facing fintech product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (surfaced under Battery Ventures).

companies.name: Home Trust
companies.description: Home Trust Company is a federally regulated Canadian trust company founded in 1977 and headquartered in Toronto, and the principal operating subsidiary of Home Capital Group. Home Capital was taken private by Smith Financial Corporation (Stephen Smith) in 2023, and the group now spans Home Trust, Home Bank (a Schedule I bank), Fairstone Bank, and the Oaken Financial deposit brand, positioning itself as one of Canada's leading alternative (non-prime) lenders. Its products include residential and commercial mortgages, reverse mortgages, Equityline, Preferred and Secured Visa credit cards, and Oaken GIC and high-interest savings deposits. Home Trust operates no public developer portal or first-party API: developer.hometrust.ca and api.hometrust.ca do not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN), no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is published, and no Interac e-Transfer or Payments Canada Real-Time Rail (RTR) API surface is documented. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, FCAC as overseer) but not yet operational, and Home Trust publishes no stated CDB or FDX position; any consumer data access today would be via screen-scraping aggregators such as Flinks or Plaid rather than a first-party API. This is an identity-only record: no public API exists as of July 2026.

companies.name: Spring Labs
companies.description: Spring Labs is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial institutions, deploying autonomous AI agents that complete operational work rather than only surfacing insights. Its agents score customer-service calls, run 100% QA/QC review coverage, identify and file complaints, and (soon) automate the dispute lifecycle, alongside SummerGRC, an AI-driven governance, risk, and compliance product. Spring Labs targets sponsor banks, fintech lenders, enterprise banks, BaaS platforms, and debt-collection (ARM) organizations. Originally a blockchain-based data and identity company backed by Multicoin Capital, the firm has repositioned around applied AI for regulated financial operations. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a marketing/product site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Tweezr
companies.description: Tweezr is a system-intelligence platform for safe legacy change, helping banks and insurers understand and incrementally evolve legacy core systems without risky big-bang modernization. The platform maps mainframe and heritage codebases (COBOL, PL/I, CICS, IMS, DB2 z/OS, VSAM, IBM i RPG, Adabas/Natural) into a deterministic, queryable, cited model that grounds engineering teams and AI tools in what the code actually does before anything is changed. Tweezr deploys on-premise by default, is a member of the Banking Industry Architecture Network (BIAN), partners with 10x Banking, is distributed through AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource, and is a Techstars portfolio company. Tweezr publishes no public API or developer program as of July 2026.

companies.name: Juno
companies.description: Juno is a Brazilian B2B payments fintech, acquired by EBANX in October 2021, that provides a complete billing and payments platform for Brazilian companies. Founded in 2014 in Maringá, Paraná, Juno powers more than 35,000 small and medium businesses with online sales and collections via Pix, boleto bancário, boleto_pix, and credit cards, plus marketplace payment split, recurring subscriptions, and a digital business account (Conta Juno) with Banking-as-a-Service capabilities. Juno is a participant of the Brazilian Interbank Payments Chamber (CIP). The company exposes a public REST API v2 through the Juno Developer Academy at integracao.juno.com.br, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials, plus HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks and native mobile Direct Checkout SDKs for Android and iOS for PCI-safe card data encryption.

companies.name: Stone Co
companies.description: Stone Co. (NASDAQ: STNE) is a Brazilian financial services and payment technology company headquartered in São Paulo. Stone provides card acquiring (POS), digital banking, business management software, and credit products to entrepreneurs and small-to-medium businesses across more than 5,500 Brazilian cities, and is the fourth-largest acquirer in Brazil following its acquisition of Elavon's Brazilian operations. Stone operates several developer-facing platforms: Connect Stone (a POS integration API for in-store payment automation and "infinite shelf" omnichannel inventory), Stone Open Banking (a RESTful banking API for account, balance, TED, PIX, and payment-link operations against Stone accounts and consented third-party accounts), the Stone SDK Android (for embedding card-present payments into Android apps and Pinpad/POS devices), AutoTEF (PIN-pad-based self-service TEF integration), the Conciliação Stone XML reconciliation feed, and Pagar.me (Stone's online/PSP gateway covering orders, charges, customers, subscriptions, split payments, recurring billing, tokenization, and 3DS). Authentication is OAuth2 / PEM-keyed JWT for Open Banking and API-key / credential-based for the other surfaces. Onboarding for Open Banking and Connect Stone partners is gated through Stone's partnerships team; Pagar.me and the Android SDK are self-service. Documentation is primarily in Portuguese and concentrated at docs.stone.com.br, docs.openbank.stone.com.br, connect-stone.stone.com.br, conciliacao.stone.com.br, and docs.pagar.me.

companies.name: Aella Credit
companies.description: Aella (Aella Credit) is a technology-driven microfinance bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), building consumer and business financial infrastructure across Africa. Its consumer app offers savings, low-interest and same-day loans, bill payments, and high-yield savings accounts, while its Fintech-as-a-Service platform exposes that infrastructure to businesses through a developer-facing API gateway. Published API capabilities include wallet-as-a- service (create and manage digital wallets with real-time balances and full ledger support), KYC/identity verification via BVN and NIN, bank-account lookup and validation, sub-accounts and pooled fund structures for platforms and marketplaces, and direct-debit recurring collections. A live Aella Merchant API is hosted at api.aellaapp.com and a merchant dashboard at merchant.aellaapp.com, though the provider does not yet publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile was seeded as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Alpharank
companies.description: Alpharank is a no-code sales guidance and digital-origination analytics platform for banks and credit unions. It analyzes funded loan and deposit applications to reveal which marketing tactics, channels, and campaigns actually drive funded dollars, then guides institutions to optimize their online branch, curb funnel abandonment, and turn ad spend into higher-quality leads. Its products include Optimizer, AdSync, and CRMSync, and it serves roughly 200 financial institutions nationwide. Originally recognized for turning payment transaction data into customer influence graphs, Alpharank is a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Alpharank publishes a marketing and client-login presence but no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: SchoolsFirst FCU
companies.description: SchoolsFirst Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Tustin, California, serving educators and their families. Founded in 1934 as Orange County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in California and one of the largest in the United States, with roughly $31.9 billion in assets, over 1.4 million members, and about 70 branches. It offers savings, checking, loans, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services. Like most US credit unions, SchoolsFirst runs no first-party public developer program: probes of developer.schoolsfirstfcu.org fail to resolve and /developers returns 404, and its api.schoolsfirstfcu.org host is the member online-banking login backend, not a documented API. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity, MX, Akoya) rather than a direct API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented at this time.

companies.name: caimitech
companies.description: caimitech.com is the domain of Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co.), a Chinese personal-finance and wealth-management company founded in 2009 that offers accounting/bookkeeping apps, personal financial management (PFM) tools, wealth-management services, and credit solutions. Its developer surface is the Wacai Open Platform (挖财开放平台) — an HMAC-signed API gateway addressed by (api_name, api_version) pairs rather than REST paths, with first-party client SDKs in Java (published to Maven Central under com.wacai), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#, plus a separate topic-based message gateway (pull/ack). Access uses an app_key/app_secret credential with MAC or RSA request signing and an optional token service. No OpenAPI document is published; this profile was enriched from the provider's public GitHub SDKs and package registries.

companies.name: Cullen/Frost Bankers
companies.description: Cullen/Frost Bankers is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cullen/Frost Bankers API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Fintech
companies.description: Fin (fin.tech) is a crypto-native payments company that lets users and businesses move millions of dollars instantly — to other Fin users, directly into bank accounts, or across crypto rails. It provides business-grade payment rails that feel like a consumer payment app rather than crypto: instant global settlement in seconds, native support to deposit and withdraw to bank accounts, and send/receive of USDT, USDC, ETH, and BTC, while Fin abstracts the underlying crypto settlement behind a clean fintech interface. Backed by Sequoia, Multicoin, and Pantera Capital, Fin operates a private, auth-gated production API surface (api.fin.tech) and publishes an llms.txt for agents; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Pantera Capital portfolio company (sector: crypto) and enriched from its public web surface.

companies.name: Pollinate
companies.description: Pollinate is a London-headquartered financial technology company that builds a cloud-based, bank-grade digital experience platform helping banks and payment processors reinvent merchant acquiring and value-added services for their small and medium business (SMB) customers. The platform wraps around a bank's legacy payment systems to deliver dynamic merchant onboarding, a bank-branded Merchant Command Center dashboard (transaction reconciliation, dispute management, statements, service discovery), integrated merchant services inside online banking, and ISV enablement. Built on Microsoft Azure and open-banking ready, it powers live bank deployments including Tyl by NatWest (UK), NAB Hive (Australia), and Tyl by CIBC (Canada), with clients including Truist and partners including Fiserv, Endava, and Dun & Bradstreet. Pollinate's APIs are private and partner-facing; it does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

companies.name: EFEX (Ventu)
companies.description: EFEX (efex.com, formerly efexpay.com) is a cross-border payments and treasury fintech serving businesses across the Americas. It enables international transfers to 140+ countries, bulk and mass payouts for payroll and multi-beneficiary disbursement, multi-currency business accounts (USD, MXN, EUR, GBP, CAD, JPY), international collections in local currency across 24+ countries, and FX and currency management for treasury optimization. Headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations across Mexico (Mexico City, Monterrey, Tijuana, Queretaro, Guadalajara) and Colombia, EFEX is authorized by Mexico's CNBV as a money transmitter (registration 22469) and regulated by FinCEN in the United States. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes a business web/app product but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

companies.name: Warbler Labs Incorporated
companies.description: Warbler Labs is the San Francisco-based software company founded in 2020 by former Coinbase engineers Blake West and Mike Sall that builds and maintains Goldfinch, a decentralized credit protocol on Ethereum for stablecoin lending to real-world borrowers without crypto collateral, and UID (Unique Identity), a KYC/KYB-compliant on-chain identity credential. Warbler Labs is the core development team behind the Goldfinch protocol, its smart contracts, oracles, and subgraph data layer, and publishes developer documentation for building on and integrating with the protocol. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coinbase Ventures, IDEO CoLab, Kindred Ventures, and others, and was surfaced through the a16z portfolio. Its developer surface is primarily on-chain (Solidity smart contracts, The Graph subgraph for querying protocol data, and the UID credential) rather than a hosted REST API.

companies.name: Fidor Bank
companies.description: Fidor Bank was a German digital challenger bank founded in Munich in 2009 and an early pioneer of Banking-as-a-Service and open banking through its fidorOS / bankOS middleware platform and public REST API, which covered Customers, Accounts, Transfers, Transactions and Account Information over an OAuth2 authorization-code flow. Fidor was acquired by France's Groupe BPCE in 2016; following years of post-acquisition integration struggles the bank ceased business operations in mid-2023 and entered liquidation. Its developer portal (fidor.com) is now a parked domain and the sandbox and production API hosts are offline. The surviving first-party developer artifacts are the archived official Ruby client (RubyGems: fidor_api, by Fidor Solutions AG) and the github.com/fidor organization. This is a retired provider retained for historical reference.

companies.name: Porters
companies.description: Porters is an AI-native outsourcing partner for European banking operations. Its platform uses AI agents with human oversight to automate high-volume back-office banking processes — account seizure processing (private and public account seizures), insolvency case management from intake to resolution, and chargeback dispute data collection, triage, and resolution. Documents are ingested, extracted, and classified; decisions are made with a human in the loop; and banking actions plus audit reports are generated automatically. Porters hosts data in the EU in line with GDPR, maintains 24/7 audit trails, and does not use customer data for model training. It was founded by veterans of McKinsey, Qonto, Upvest, Solaris, and Roland Berger, and is backed by Earlybird and Seedcamp. No public developer API is currently published.

companies.name: Vixtra
companies.description: Vixtra (VIXTRA Tecnologia e Serviços Financeiros LTDA., CNPJ 43.443.444/0001-04) is a Brazilian trade-finance fintech founded in July 2021 and headquartered in São Paulo, positioning itself as "the Trade Banking of the Brazilian importer." It pioneers financing for importers using in-transit maritime cargo as collateral, and delivers credit, foreign exchange, guarantees, and cash-flow management for foreign trade from a single digital platform. Its products include Crédito Flex (revolving working-capital credit), Crédito Pré (pre-shipment import financing), Câmbio Fácil (100% digital commercial FX), Trade Banking (the unified operations platform), and a Vixtra stablecoin for cross-border payments. Vixtra operates as a banking correspondent of BMP Money Plus SCD and an FX correspondent of Ebury Banco de Câmbio, has raised roughly US$36M (US$30M debt + US$6M seed extension) led by QED Investors with Valor Capital Group, Endeavor Promessas, NXTP Ventures, Actyus, and BluStone, and processes data in compliance with Brazil's LGPD. No public developer portal or API is currently published; the api.vixtra.com host backs the customer application and returns 403 to anonymous callers.

companies.name: Nymbus
companies.description: Nymbus is a Jacksonville, Florida-based fintech software provider delivering cloud-based core banking, digital banking, and account onboarding technology to community banks and credit unions. Its Nymbus Connect product exposes a modern RESTful API layer alongside a client- and partner-facing developer portal, a secure sandbox environment, real-time Kafka event streaming (event-driven architecture), and an AWS-based data lake and Redshift data warehouse for reporting and analytics. Nymbus is backed by Insight Partners. The public developer portal and API reference are gated to authenticated clients and partners, so no public OpenAPI specification is available at this time.

companies.name: Texas Capital Bank
companies.description: Texas Capital Bank, National Association is the banking subsidiary of Texas Capital Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: TCBI), a Dallas-headquartered full-service financial services firm founded in 1998 with roughly $31.5 billion in assets (FYE 2025). As a nationally chartered commercial bank it serves businesses, entrepreneurs, and institutions across Texas and the United States with commercial and business banking, treasury management, mortgage/warehouse finance, and investment banking. On the open-finance dimension the bank is relationship-first rather than developer-first: it markets treasury and ERP API integrations (including its ConnectNow embedded banking for Sage and NetSuite, direct platform integrations, and SFTP/XChange file transfer) but exposes them through partner onboarding with dedicated bankers, not a public self-serve developer portal. There is no public first-party developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no self-serve API signup. Consumer account and transaction data is made available to permissioned third parties through the Finicity (Mastercard) aggregator rather than a first-party API, which is the honest posture for most US regional banks under the voluntary, fragmented US open-banking landscape (CFPB Section 1033 and the industry FDX standard).

companies.name: Columbia Bank
companies.description: Columbia Bank is an Oregon state-chartered commercial bank and the principal banking subsidiary of Columbia Banking System, Inc. (NASDAQ: COLB), a West Coast regional bank holding company headquartered in Tacoma, Washington with more than $50 billion in assets. The bank took the legal name "Columbia Bank" effective July 1, 2025, having previously operated as Umpqua Bank following the 2023 merger of Columbia Banking System and Umpqua Holdings Corporation. On the open-finance front, Columbia is one of the relatively few US regional banks to run a first-party developer surface: Columbia API Banking, a commercial and treasury-management integration product exposing capabilities such as book transfers, ACH file imports, positive pay, stop-payment and NSF management, lockbox management, transaction and statement search, check images, and real-time account balances in JSON and XML, backed by a production-ready SDK and the gated Columbia API Portal. That surface is commercial/ERP-oriented rather than a self-serve public developer portal, and consumer-permissioned data access is instead delivered through the Plaid aggregator. No documented FDX participation or published CFPB Section 1033 posture was found.

companies.name: HSBC
companies.description: One of the world's largest banking and financial services organizations headquartered in London. Serves over 40 million customers globally with a strong presence in Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Operates a public Developer Portal (develop.hsbc.com) exposing Open Banking, payments, accounts, and global payments solutions APIs for partners and third-party providers.

companies.name: Kuda
companies.description: Kuda is a Nigerian digital-first retail bank — branded "the money app for Africans" and "the bank of the free" — founded in 2019 by Babs Ogundeyi and Musty Mustapha and headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria with operations in the United Kingdom. Kuda's Nigerian entity, Kuda Microfinance Bank, holds a national microfinance bank license from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), and Kuda EMI Limited operates as an FCA-authorised electronic money institution in the UK. Kuda offers retail banking accounts with zero or low fees, debit cards, instant transfers, bill payments, savings ("Spend+Save"), investments, overdrafts, and personal loans through its iOS, Android, and web apps, plus a Business banking suite covering expense accounts and cards, payroll, invoicing, softPOS and physical POS terminals, business loans, and CAC business registration. Kuda also exposes an Open API ("Kuda Open API") aimed at fintechs, marketplaces, and businesses that want to embed Nigerian banking primitives — virtual accounts, name enquiry, intra- and inter-bank transfers, balance inquiry, transaction history, bill payments, and disbursements — directly into their own products, with sandbox and live environments, RSA-encrypted request payloads, and client libraries for Node.js, PHP, C#, Rust, and Kotlin hosted under the kudabank GitHub organization.

companies.name: Pollen
companies.description: Pollen Technologies is a London-based, FCA-authorised white-label fintech platform that lets any business launch its own banking and payments product with no code and a fully managed back office. The platform delivers programmatic payment delivery, instant named IBAN account opening, third-party bank account linking for real-time balances and transaction data, multi-currency payments across 148 currencies into more than 160 countries, local payment schemes, and virtual and physical cards. A managed compliance layer covers KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, client fund safeguarding and help-desk support under SLAs. Pollen Technologies Ltd is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (firm reference 768011), founded in 2015 and backed by Seedcamp, Level39 and Q-Advisers. Access to the underlying payments and banking APIs is delivered as a managed, partner-only service rather than a public self-serve developer program, so no public API specifications, SDKs or developer portal are currently published.

companies.name: ATB Financial
companies.description: ATB Financial (formerly Alberta Treasury Branches) is a financial institution and Crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of Alberta, established in 1938 and operating under the provincial ATB Financial Act rather than the federal Bank Act. Headquartered in Edmonton, it is Alberta's largest home-grown financial institution and the largest public bank in North America, with roughly C$64 billion in assets, more than 800,000 customers, about 5,000 team members, and 300+ branches and agencies across the province; deposits are guaranteed by the Province of Alberta rather than covered by CDIC. On the open-finance front, ATB does NOT operate a public first-party developer portal or documented public API surface (developer.atb.com returns HTTP 404), and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational. Consumer financial-data access to ATB today is therefore voluntary and aggregator-mediated — reached through third-party aggregators such as Finicity (by Mastercard) and Flinks rather than a direct bank API.

companies.name: Rabobank
companies.description: Rabobank is a Dutch multinational banking and financial services company organized as a cooperative with a strong focus on the food and agriculture sector. It serves retail, business, corporate, and wholesale customers in the Netherlands and operates a global Food & Agribusiness practice through Rabobank Wholesale & Rural and the Rabobank Group internationally. Rabobank publishes a developer portal at docs.developer.rabobank.com (legacy URL developer.rabobank.nl redirects there) exposing PSD2-mandated open banking APIs (Account Information, Payment Initiation, Funds Confirmation) as well as Premium / Beyond-PSD2 commercial APIs for corporate cash management and notifications, with sandbox endpoints for development and a regulated production tier under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Underlying schemes are aligned with the Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 XS2A Framework.

companies.name: Transbnk
companies.description: TransBnk — rebranded as TBX — is an Indian open-finance and transaction-banking infrastructure company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Mumbai. It gives banks, enterprises, fintechs, corporates, and NBFCs the platforms, APIs, and connected workflows behind corporate banking: mandate management, escrow flows, virtual accounts, reconciliation, lending acceleration, and cash and treasury management. TransBnk reports partnerships with 25+ banks, 200+ APIs extended, 100+ BFSI clients, and 50M+ transactions processed. Products include TxB Hub (transaction banking), TrustHub (core banking and escrow), and the API Hub integration surface. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, 8i Ventures, and Accion Venture Lab.

companies.name: Flagstar
companies.description: Flagstar Bank, N.A. is the OCC-chartered national bank subsidiary of Flagstar Financial, Inc. (NYSE: FLG), the Hicksville, New York holding company formerly known as New York Community Bancorp (NYCB). It is one of the largest regional (super-regional) banks in the United States, formed when NYCB acquired Flagstar Bancorp in December 2022, converted Flagstar Bank, FSB into a national bank (Flagstar Bank, N.A.), and subsequently acquired certain assets and liabilities of Signature Bridge Bank from the FDIC in March 2023; the holding company rebranded to Flagstar Financial in October 2024. Flagstar operates in retail and commercial banking, mortgage origination and servicing, and warehouse lending. On the API front, Flagstar runs a first-party developer portal at developer.flagstar.com (a Broadcom/Layer7 "LivePortal" API Developer Portal), but as of this review it publishes no public, self-serve API products, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger to anonymous visitors — all products are sign-in gated behind partner/consumer-team access. Flagstar has no publicly documented FDX (Financial Data Exchange) participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture; consumer-permissioned data sharing appears to be available only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, Tink, TrueLayer) rather than a first-party public API.

companies.name: Oportun
companies.description: Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company and U.S. Treasury-certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) that provides responsible, affordable personal loans, savings, and budgeting tools to people with limited or no credit history. Founded in 2006, Oportun has disbursed more than $20.8 billion across 7.7 million loans and established credit history for over 1.3 million people. Beyond its consumer app, Oportun runs an Enterprise Platform offering Lending-as-a-Service (LaaS) and embedded-finance partnerships, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-serve API; the LaaS integration API is available only through contact-gated enterprise partnerships.

companies.name: Sav Technologies Limited
companies.description: Sav Technologies Limited operates Sav (sav.money), a UAE-based intelligent financial platform that lets users track, save, invest, and grow their wealth across accounts. Sav offers a suite of consumer products including Gold (physical gold investment from AED 10), MyMoney (financial management and savings), Card (a prepaid card with cashback), Wealth (investing), Sav Pro (premium membership), and an upcoming Credit product. Sav describes itself as extending the APIs and technology components of licensed financial services providers to its users. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Sav publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: TomoCredit
companies.description: TomoCredit is a consumer fintech that helps people build credit without requiring a credit score or prior credit history. Its flagship products are the Tomo Card, a credit-building card marketed as an all-new black card, and TomoBoost, an AI-powered credit-building tool. The company positions itself around fast approval (apply in minutes), no credit-history requirement, and cardmember benefits and coverage it values at over $1,300, aiming to help thin-file consumers such as newcomers and students establish and grow their credit. TomoCredit was surfaced through the Techstars portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Velotax
companies.description: Velotax is a Brazilian digital-credit fintech (mobile app plus velotax.com.br), operating 100% online, that offers unsecured personal loans and income-tax (IRPF) refund advances, disbursed via Pix within 30 minutes of approval — approving even "negativado" (poor-credit) customers because the anticipated tax refund secures repayment. Founded in 2020 by ex-J.P. Morgan bankers Eduardo Esmanhotto and Victor Savioli, it operates as a banking correspondent in partnership with VIA CAPITAL (a Brazilian Central Bank SCD), holds Reclame Aqui's top RA1000 reputation seal, has 3M+ app downloads, and raised a R$125M Series A in 2025 from QED Investors, Valor Capital and Picus Capital. Velotax is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Anchor Protocol
companies.description: Anchor Protocol is a Terra-based decentralized finance (DeFi) savings protocol that offered a low-volatility yield on Terra stablecoin (UST) deposits, borrowing against bonded-asset (bAsset) collateral such as bLUNA and bETH, and cross-chain access through EthAnchor and xAnchor. Its developer surface is a set of first-party JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs (Anchor.js and Anchor Earn) plus on-chain CosmWasm smart contracts rather than a REST or OpenAPI web API. The project is part of the Terra ecosystem and is backed by Pantera Capital; its main web application deployment is currently disabled, though its developer documentation and npm SDK packages remain published.

companies.name: Western Alliance Bancorp.
companies.description: Western Alliance Bancorporation is a bank holding company headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, that provides commercial banking, treasury management, and specialty lending services through Western Alliance Bank. The company serves business clients across multiple regional and national specialty segments. Western Alliance Bancorp does not publish a public developer API portal.

companies.name: Divine
companies.description: Divine Research Inc. is a fintech company building blockchain-based unsecured lending for underserved borrowers in emerging markets. Its flagship product, Credit, issues small stablecoin (USDC) loans that start small and can grow to $1,000 as borrowers build trust, with algorithmically set interest rates and default rates that have approached zero. Borrowers access loans through a World MiniApp, while liquidity providers supply capital and earn yield through the Credit Vault at credit.cash. As of late 2024 the platform had issued hundreds of thousands of loans to more than 500,000 borrowers. Divine is backed by Paradigm and was surfaced through its portfolio; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network. Divine currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

companies.name: Aven
companies.description: Aven is a consumer fintech that issues a home-equity-backed Visa credit card, letting homeowners tap their home equity (a HELOC) through a card with credit-card convenience at lower, home-equity-secured rates. Its product line spans the Aven HELOC card, a Bitcoin-backed Visa card, and educational tooling such as a payment calculator, positioning itself as an AI-driven "machine bank." Founded in the fintech sector and backed by Electric Capital, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, GGV Capital, and Khosla Ventures, Aven operates a consumer marketing and account-servicing web presence at aven.com. As of this enrichment pass Aven publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: BOK Financial
companies.description: BOK Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: BOKF) is a regional financial-services holding company headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, delivering banking under the Bank of Oklahoma, Bank of Texas, and BOK Financial brands across the Southwest and Midwest, along with wealth management and commercial treasury services. As of July 2026 it does not publish a first-party public developer portal or any documented API products — developer.bokfinancial.com does not resolve and /developer and /api return 404. Its public, machine-accessible surface is consumer-permissioned account data access delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid coverage confirmed), while commercial treasury and ERP connectivity is offered privately to clients under contract rather than through a self-serve documented developer program.

companies.name: Cit Vericash
companies.description: CIT Vericash is a fintech enablement platform from CIT Global (founded in Toronto, Canada in 1993) that empowers banks, neo banks, microfinance institutions, and fintechs to launch and operate digital financial services. Its high-configuration, no-code/low-code VERICASH platform delivers digital banking, agency banking, digital payments, and mobile wallet capabilities across an omnichannel surface (mobile, USSD, web, and agent networks), with AI-powered customer intelligence and fraud prevention. The platform is live across roughly 25 markets in Africa and the Middle East, serving banked and unbanked communities to advance financial inclusion in emerging markets. CIT Vericash is a portfolio company of Anthemis and was added to the API Evangelist network from the VC portfolio pipeline.

companies.name: Infosys
companies.description: Infosys is a global IT services, consulting, and outsourcing company headquartered in Bengaluru, India, providing digital transformation, cloud, AI, and business process services. Through its Finacle banking software product and Banking API Platform, Infosys exposes open banking APIs for deposits, loans, payments, trade finance, and data privacy, along with a configurable developer portal, API composer, and consent management. A public Finacle Open Bank Project sandbox is also available for developers to explore banking APIs.

companies.name: Magicpin
companies.description: Magicpin (operated by Samast Technologies Private Limited) is India's hyperlocal savings and discovery platform, connecting consumers with deals, cashback, and vouchers across restaurants, food delivery, fashion, grocery, beauty, fitness, and electronics merchants in cities throughout India. The company operates a consumer savings app alongside a merchant/brands portal and corporate voucher solutions. As of this enrichment pass Magicpin publishes a consumer web and mobile experience plus partner and brand onboarding portals, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Randolph-Brooks FCU
companies.description: Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union (RBFCU) is a member-owned, not-for-profit federal credit union headquartered in Live Oak, Texas, federally insured by the NCUA and serving more than one million members across Texas and beyond. Chartered as a federal credit union rather than a state or national bank, RBFCU is one of the largest credit unions in the United States by membership and assets, offering retail banking, mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and deposit products through branches and digital channels. As a member-focused retail institution, RBFCU publishes no first-party public developer program, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, or Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API, and it publishes no stated CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture or documented FDX participation.

companies.name: Yo Fio
companies.description: YoFio is a Mexican fintech founded in 2019 that provides working-capital credit to micro and small businesses, particularly neighborhood corner stores (tienditas). Through a mobile app and web platform it offers revolving credit lines of 7,000 to 200,000 Mexican pesos with up to 14 days of interest-free financing so merchants can restock inventory and pay suppliers. YoFio uses AI-powered machine-vision technology to assess creditworthiness from photos and videos of a store and its inventory, cutting the evaluation process to roughly 15 minutes. It is backed by 500 Global and Oikocredit, and serves thousands of businesses across the Valley of Mexico, Puebla, and Guadalajara. YoFio publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

companies.name: Bachatt
companies.description: Bachatt is a daily savings and investments mobile app operated by Trusave Fintech Private Limited, designed for India's underserved and self-employed population. As an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor, Bachatt lets users save from as little as INR 100/day and invest in liquid mutual funds (Insta Fund) with instant withdrawal, curated mutual fund baskets (Bachatt Wealth), gold and silver mutual funds, fixed deposits, and access instant personal and business loans (Insta Loans) up to INR 5 lakhs. The company partners with major AMCs including SBI, ICICI Prudential, Axis, and HDFC and delivers everything through a single UPI-powered mobile application on Android and iOS. Bachatt is backed by Accel. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Bachatt is a consumer fintech app and does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Finda
companies.description: Finda (핀다) is a South Korean fintech company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Seoul that operates a licensed online loan-comparison and financial-product marketplace. Through its mobile app and website, Finda lets consumers compare loan products from 76+ financial institutions and 400+ products in about a minute, refinance existing loans ("갈아타기"), aggregate accounts and cards for asset management, run financial calculators (interest, DSR, year-end tax, mortgage eligibility), and monitor and manage their credit. Registered as a loan-brokerage/loan-collection corporation under Korea's Financial Services Act, Finda earns commissions from partner financial institutions rather than charging consumers. It reports 3.47M+ cumulative members and 256T+ won in managed loan assets, and is backed by 500 Global. Finda is a consumer B2C platform and does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Wollit
companies.description: Wollit is a UK-based credit-health subscription service (£9.99/month) that helps consumers build and strengthen their credit profile. Authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority for credit-broking activities, Wollit reports rent and subscription payments to Experian, Equifax and TransUnion, and bundles a suite of consumer tools: Rent Reporting, Payment Reporting, an AI credit assistant (Olli), Affordability Boost, Credit Smart lessons, and Credit Wins. It is a consumer-facing fintech app and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Brookfield Asset Management
companies.description: Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE: BAM, TSX: BAM) is a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion in assets under management and approximately $614 billion in fee-bearing capital. BAM describes itself as "a pure-play, asset-light investment manager with earnings derived from stable, predictable fee-related revenue." The publicly listed manager was formed in December 2022 when it was spun out of Brookfield Corporation (NYSE: BN), which remains the majority shareholder. BAM operates across five investment verticals — Renewable Power & Transition, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Private Equity, and Credit — and adjacent Insurance Solutions capability is delivered through Brookfield Wealth Solutions, a sister business within the broader Brookfield ecosystem. BAM does not publish a public developer API program. Institutional Limited Partners, financial intermediaries, distribution platforms, and portfolio companies interact with the firm through private, authentication-gated investor portals, PDF reporting (10-K, supplemental, letters to shareholders), data feeds from fund administrators, and the investor-relations website at bam.brookfield.com.

companies.name: CashDirector
companies.description: CashDirector is a fintech platform delivering AI-powered financial management for small businesses through a white-label, B2B2C partner model. It embeds banking and accounting automation directly into financial institutions' online banking platforms so banks can offer their SME clients a "beyond banking" daily digital business assistant. The platform automates invoicing, expense tracking, cash flow forecasting and receivables management, using AI and OCR to process financial documents automatically. It supports multibanking with minimal IT involvement and reports over 250,000 users across partnerships with six major European banks, positioning itself as Europe's first online accounting system with full banking integration. CashDirector is a Techstars portfolio company; it publishes no public developer portal or open API surface — integration is delivered privately to bank partners.

companies.name: Pinnacle Financial
companies.description: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc. (NASDAQ: PNFP) is a Nashville, Tennessee based regional bank holding company whose principal subsidiary, Pinnacle Bank, is a Tennessee state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #35583) originally founded in 2000 as Pinnacle National Bank and renamed in 2012. Pinnacle operates across the Southeast — Tennessee, the Carolinas, Virginia, Georgia and Alabama — serving consumer, small-business, commercial and wealth clients. On the open-finance side Pinnacle runs NO public first-party developer API portal; its consumer digital and mobile banking is delivered on a third-party core/digital platform (Apiture), and consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available to fintechs only through data aggregators (Plaid and Finicity/Mastercard) rather than through a documented bank-operated API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found; open-finance participation is aggregator-mediated.

companies.name: Prospera Credit Union
companies.description: Prospera Credit Union is a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in British Columbia, Canada, formed on January 1, 2020 through the merger of the original Prospera Credit Union and Westminster Savings Credit Union — the largest credit-union merger in Canadian history. With roughly CA$9 billion in assets under management, about 120,000 members, and some 900 employees across branches in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, and the Okanagan, it is the third largest credit union in British Columbia and among the six largest in Canada. As a provincially regulated cooperative (credit unions in BC are overseen by BC Financial Services Authority and deposits are protected by the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation of BC), Prospera serves personal and business members with chequing and savings accounts, credit cards, mortgages, loans, and Interac e-Transfer. On the open-finance side, Prospera runs NO public first-party developer portal or documented API — none of developer/api/developers.prospera.ca resolve — and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and overseen by the FCAC, is not yet operational. Like most Canadian credit unions, Prospera reaches national payment rails and consumer data-sharing through shared credit-union-system infrastructure rather than a proprietary API, and third-party data access today is aggregator/screen-scraping based (e.g. Flinks, Plaid). This is an honest identity-only profile with no public API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Scalable Capital
companies.description: Scalable Capital is a Munich-based digital investment platform and licensed bank operating across Germany, Austria, Italy, France, Spain and the Netherlands. It offers a self-directed neobroker for trading stocks, ETFs, bonds, funds, crypto and derivatives, automated Wealth (robo-advisory) portfolio management, ETF and stock savings plans, an interest-bearing overnight cash account, and credit services. Backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, Scalable Capital serves retail investors through consumer web and mobile applications; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via public-surface probes.

companies.name: Niyo Solutions
companies.description: Niyo Solutions (brand: Niyo, goniyo.com) is a Bengaluru, India based consumer fintech founded in 2015 by Vinay Bagri and Virender Bisht, focused on international travel banking and savings for Indian retail customers. Niyo is not a chartered bank; it operates as a neo-banking front end layered on partner RBI-licensed banks — DCB Bank (current flagship for the Niyo zero-forex savings + debit card), SBM Bank India (previous "Niyo Global" forex card, now wound down for new customers and operating a secured credit card variant), Equitas Small Finance Bank (salary / "Niyo Bharat" account) and IDFC FIRST Bank (earlier Niyo Global issuer) — plus card network rails (Visa, RuPay). Niyo's flagship surface is the "zero forex markup" Niyo Global / DCB Niyo Global / SBM Niyo Global Visa debit and prepaid travel cards accepted in 180+ countries, paired with a digital savings account delivered through partner banks. The company has expanded beyond cards into a full travel-banking stack including currency exchange and forex cash delivery, outbound remittance (Send Money Abroad), international flights, hotels and curated experiences, Niyo Express airport services, an international travel eSIM, travel visa assistance, travel insurance, a premium subscription tier, a student program (Niyo Scholarship, NISAP) and a DCB Niyo Secured Credit Card backed by a fixed deposit. Niyo serves over one million international travellers and has raised capital from investors including Accel, Lightrock, Beams Fintech Fund, Tencent, Horizons Ventures, Prime Venture Partners and JS Capital. There is no public REST developer API, partner banking-as-a-service surface, SDK, MCP server, or GitHub organisation — Niyo is delivered exclusively as a B2C iOS and Android mobile application with a marketing and tools website at goniyo.com.

companies.name: TD Bank Group
companies.description: TD Bank Group (The Toronto-Dominion Bank) is one of Canada's Big Six chartered banks — a federally regulated Schedule I bank headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX and NYSE under the ticker TD. It is among North America's largest banks by assets, serving roughly 27 million customers worldwide across Canadian Personal & Commercial Banking (TD Canada Trust), U.S. Retail (TD Bank, N.A. — America's Most Convenient Bank, a separately profiled entity), and Wholesale Banking (TD Securities). Like the rest of Canada's banking sector, TD's open-finance posture is voluntary: Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework was legislated in 2024 (Consumer-Driven Banking Act) but is not yet operational, so the Canadian parent exposes no first-party public developer API. Consumer financial-data access today is aggregator-based — TD signed a North American data-access agreement with Plaid in December 2023 — while payments run over the shared Canadian rails (Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail, with Interac as the RTR exchange solution provider). The FDX-aligned, Akoya-based open-banking API suite published at developer.td.com belongs to the U.S. subsidiary TD Bank, N.A., not this Canadian entity.

companies.name: Arro
companies.description: Arro is a consumer fintech company that helps people build or rebuild credit without traditional barriers. Its flagship product is the Arro Card, a Mastercard with no deposit and no hard credit check that starts at up to $300 and grows to $2,500, issued by Community Federal Savings Bank (member FDIC). The Arro app pairs the card with financial-education lessons, credit tracking, personalized guidance, and Artie, an AI money coach. Arro is a mobile-first consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Deben
companies.description: Deben is an AI-powered treasury and cash management platform for CFOs and finance teams, positioned as a cloud-native alternative to spreadsheets and legacy treasury management systems. The product covers cash management with centralized bank connectivity and multi-currency support, liquidity planning and forecasting, automated bank and payment reconciliation, payments, banking and ERP connectivity, multi-entity consolidation, and debt management, with an emphasis on real-time cash control and AI-driven forecasting. Deben targets finance teams in Saudi Arabia and the wider region, referencing Open Banking, and is backed by 500 Global. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; Deben does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface, so this record captures company identity and probed domain security only.

companies.name: Citi
companies.description: Citi is the consumer-facing brand of Citigroup, the global diversified financial services holding company. The Citi developer surface is cataloged under the canonical Citigroup profile, which covers the Citi Developer Hub, retail Accounts and Transactions, Money Movement, Authorization, Customer Onboarding, Pay with Points, Utilities, and CitiConnect for corporate treasury. This entry exists as an alias so the citi short name resolves to the same catalog as citigroup.
