companies.name: ING
companies.description: A Dutch multinational banking and financial services corporation headquartered in Amsterdam. Provides retail banking, direct banking, commercial banking, and wholesale banking services to millions of customers across Europe and globally. Operates a public Developer Portal exposing Open Banking, PSD2, and payment-related APIs for third-party developers and fintech partners.

companies.name: Lydia
companies.description: Lydia is a French fintech, founded in 2013, that built one of Europe's most popular mobile peer-to-peer payments apps, letting users send money, split bills, and pay merchants from their phone. Backed by Accel, Tencent and others, the company evolved into a full mobile banking and financial services provider. In 2024 it split its consumer banking product into a new brand, Sumeria (sumeria.eu), while the Lydia name continues for the P2P payments experience. Lydia publishes a security.txt bug-bounty contact but no longer exposes a public developer API or portal.

companies.name: Onit
companies.description: Onit is a Kenyan digital bank operated by Onit Microfinance Bank Inc. and regulated by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK), with deposits protected by the Kenya Deposit Insurance Corporation (KDIC). Formerly known as Shara, Onit provides a free peer-to-peer transaction network linking consumers, businesses, and suppliers: users can send and receive money instantly and at no cost between Onit accounts, run separate personal and business accounts, and access loans and checkout/BNPL finance from a single mobile app. The company positions open APIs as part of its offering to let partners and merchants integrate consumer payments, though it does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation. Onit is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and operates in the emerging-markets fintech space.

companies.name: Text'nPayMe
companies.description: Text'nPayMe is an award-winning B2B fintech company, established in Armenia and incorporated in the USA in 2022, that builds embedded payment solutions for banks, fintechs, telecoms, and online shops. Its two core products are a Payment Keyboard SDK, which embeds send-money transactions directly inside 150+ messaging, social, and gaming apps via a payment keyboard for iOS, Android, and a Chrome extension, and a Payment Gateway Hub for transaction routing, reconciliation, and reporting. The company markets an "Apex Security Layer" with proprietary encryption and risk management, supports cross-border payments, and joined the 500 Global accelerator after winning the Entrepreneurship World Cup 2022 National Finals. The SDK is delivered to enterprise customers through direct integration engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal, so no public API specification, developer documentation, or client packages are currently published.

companies.name: Bond
companies.description: Bond Financial Technologies was an embedded-finance platform that offered APIs for card issuing (Bond Issuing), money movement (Bond Pay), deposit accounts (Bond Banking), and credit underwriting (Bond Credit) to brands and fintechs. Bond was acquired by FIS (Fidelity National Information Services) in 2023 and its product surface has been folded into Atelio by FIS at atelio.com. The original Bond developer portal and API surface at bond.tech is no longer the primary access path; new partners are routed to the Atelio platform. This is an honest historical record.

companies.name: Market IQ
companies.description: Market IQ is a predictive analytics platform for financial institutions, serving retail banking, investment banking, and capital markets. It ingests both structured and unstructured data, applies natural language processing and AI to generate insights, and delivers bespoke dashboards such as its Social Net Promoter Score and incident-monitoring tools. The company operates from Toronto, New York, and London and reaches customers through login-gated applications rather than a public developer API. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Diebold Nixdorf
companies.description: Diebold Nixdorf is a global leader in driving connected commerce for the financial and retail industries, providing self-service kiosks, ATMs, point-of-sale systems, Vynamic software, and related services. While Diebold Nixdorf operates several customer support and software portals (Aftersales Portal, eServices Portal, Manuals Drivers and Downloads), it does not currently publish a public open developer portal or open APIs. This repository is maintained as a placeholder for any APIs, developer tools, or machine-readable artifacts that may emerge.

companies.name: payflows
companies.description: Payflows is an AI-native financial operations platform that unifies procurement, treasury, and accounting into one agentic workspace for finance teams. Its product suites span Apollo (procurement from purchase request to receipt), Vera (vendor and contract management), Athena (accounting and AP automation from AP to tax reporting), and Metis (treasury from payment to bank reconciliation), with spend analytics, cashflow forecasting, global payments, and risk management. Payflows integrates with major ERP, banking, payment, and expense systems. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Tala
companies.description: Tala is an AI-native digital financial services company providing instant credit, digital wallets, money transfers, and cash-out services to underserved consumers in informal economies. Built on a proprietary, patent-pending credit-decisioning model trained on billions of dollars of lending data, Tala has delivered more than $7B in credit access to over 13 million customers across Kenya, Mexico, the Philippines, India, Vietnam, Guatemala, Panama, and the Dominican Republic. The company also offers Embedded Credit infrastructure for partners. Tala reaches customers primarily through consumer mobile apps; no public developer API or documentation portal is currently published.

companies.name: SpotPay
companies.description: SpotPay is a global neobank that operates as a stablecoin-based global bank account, letting users hold, send, receive, and spend money anywhere in the world from a single identity-verified digital wallet without a traditional bank account. The service settles payments on blockchain rails using stablecoins and pairs the wallet with the SpotPay Calypso debit card plus Apple Pay and Google Pay support, and lets merchants accept QR-code payments with instant settlement. Founded by Zsika Phillip (CEO, ex-Google) and Thomas Cesare-Herriau (CTO, ex-Brex), SpotPay is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company operating across 40+ countries and registered as a Money Services Business with FinCEN in the United States. As of this enrichment pass SpotPay is a consumer mobile-app product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; api.spotpay.ai serves only the app's private backend.

companies.name: Clinc
companies.description: Clinc is a conversational AI platform for banking and financial services, founded in 2015 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. It provides the Natural Language Understanding (NLU), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Natural Language Generation (NLG) engine behind virtual assistants and chatbots, and is ASR/TTS-agnostic so it can be connected to phone, mobile, web, or smart-speaker devices. Once a user utterance is converted to text, Clinc's AI engine interprets intent and calls the appropriate third-party systems (such as an external database) to answer or carry out an action. Clinc has been deployed with customers including USAA, Ford, Barclays, and İşbank, and is backed by Insight Partners, Drive Capital, and eLab Ventures. NOTE — Clinc's public developer surface (clinc.com and api.clinc.com) is offline as of 2026-07-18: the clinc.com AWS Route53 delegation is dangling and its authoritative nameservers return REFUSED, so the domain resolves SERVFAIL everywhere. The documentation and API URLs recorded here are the genuine published locations, recoverable via the Internet Archive.

companies.name: Ally Financial
companies.description: Ally Financial (NYSE: ALLY) is a US super-regional, all-digital bank holding company and one of the country's largest auto finance providers, offering online deposit accounts, auto and personal lending, mortgages, credit cards, and self-directed and robo brokerage through Ally Invest. Ally does not operate a live, self-serve first-party public developer portal for its consumer banking products. Programmatic access to Ally Bank account and transaction data is delivered through third-party open-finance aggregators (Plaid and Flinks are documented), and the legacy Ally Invest brokerage REST API (inherited from the 2016 TradeKing acquisition) has effectively been retired as Ally Invest shifted toward managed and robo portfolios.

companies.name: Inventa
companies.description: Inventa is a Brazilian B2B commerce platform — a "B2B commerce cloud" — that integrates technology, credit, and logistics on a single platform so brands and distributors can scale wholesale sales in Brazil. Its products include a sales platform that syncs catalogs, orders, inventory, and prices across B2B e-commerce sites and marketplaces via ERP integrations; a field-sales mobile app for sellers; automated credit analysis and approval; shared distribution-center logistics (OMS/WMS/TMS) with fulfillment and 72-hour delivery in the São Paulo region; multichannel customer support; and business-intelligence dashboards. Solution packages span Fulfillment, Response, FullService, and a pay-per-use OnDemand model. The company is headquartered in São Paulo. Inventa configures the API and connector integrations for its customers rather than publishing a public developer portal, so it has no public API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Zions Bancorporation
companies.description: Zions Bancorporation, National Association is a nationally chartered bank and bank holding company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with roughly $87 billion in total assets. It is a super-regional operating a single national bank charter across seven regional divisional brands - Zions Bank, Amegy Bank, California Bank & Trust, National Bank of Arizona, Nevada State Bank, Vectra Bank Colorado, and The Commerce Bank of Washington - serving consumers, small business, and commercial/treasury clients across the Western United States. On the open-finance front Zions runs NO public first-party developer API portal: developer.zionsbank.com and api.zionsbank.com do not resolve, and its business digital-banking surface (Treasury Internet Banking at treasurygateway.zionsbank.com) is credential-gated with no published API reference or downloadable OpenAPI. As a large depository institution it is subject to the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but Zions has not published a first-party data-access API or a documented FDX-conformant endpoint; consumer-permissioned data sharing in practice reaches Zions through third-party aggregators (Plaid/MX/Finicity/Akoya) rather than a first-party API surface.

companies.name: Zet
companies.description: Zet is a Bengaluru, India fintech that helps unserved and underserved Indians enter the formal credit system. Its core product is a fixed-deposit-backed (FD-backed) secured credit card starting at very low deposits, requiring no income proof or prior credit history, alongside credit-score monitoring and improvement tools, UPI payments, cashback rewards, a ZET Plus subscription tier, and a ZET Fixit credit-report error-resolution service. Backed by General Catalyst and Sequoia Capital, Zet operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer platform, API, OpenAPI, or documented developer surface.

companies.name: Duane Morris
companies.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

companies.name: FairMoney
companies.description: FairMoney is a credit-led digital bank for emerging markets, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Paris, France, with operating subsidiaries in Nigeria and India. The company began life as a France-incubated micro- lending app and pivoted to focus on Africa, becoming one of the largest digital lenders in Nigeria after the Central Bank of Nigeria granted its subsidiary a Microfinance Bank (MfB) license. FairMoney's consumer mobile app offers near-instant collateral-free personal loans, FlexiCredit, asset finance, savings products (FairLock, FairSave, FairTarget, FairDollar), a current account, debit cards, bill payments, and peer-to-peer transfers. Its Business Banking arm extends current accounts, payments, and credit to Nigerian SMEs. In India, FairMoney operates as a digital lender disbursing small-ticket personal loans through its mobile app. FairMoney does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a third-party developer portal; integration is internal and partner- driven, and the company's only public technical surface is its engineering GitHub organization, which mirrors infrastructure-as-code and open-source tooling forks (Terraform AWS modules, GitHub Actions, rubocop, puma plugins, salesforce_bulk_api) rather than a product API.

companies.name: Apollo Global Management
companies.description: Apollo Global Management is a global alternative investment manager providing private equity, credit, and real assets strategies to institutional and individual investors. With over $840 billion in assets under management, Apollo focuses on delivering excess returns through its private equity, credit, and real assets business segments. Apollo does not have a public developer API program.

companies.name: SlideRule
companies.description: SlideRule is a no-code risk decisioning platform that lets risk and operations teams build, test, and deploy automated decision logic for fraud, credit, compliance, and trust-and-safety use cases without writing code. Its rules engine combines SQL and API data connectors, real-time analytics, A/B testing, backtesting, shadow mode, and case-management automation, and exposes a single API to trigger decision workflows. SlideRule has announced it is joining Block, Inc.; its standalone developer documentation surface (docs.sliderule.io) is no longer publicly reachable, so no live API specification could be harvested during enrichment.

companies.name: Moven
companies.description: Moven (Movencorp Newco Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2011 by Brett King and Alex Sion. Originally a direct-to-consumer mobile banking and financial-wellness app, the company pivoted in 2020 to a business-to-business model, licensing its spending-analytics and financial-wellness technology to banks, credit unions, and other fintechs through open APIs and SDKs. Its data-driven engagement modules power companion and challenger-bank experiences such as TD Bank's MySpend and Westpac's CashNav. Moven's API and SDK surface is partner-gated behind a demo/sandbox request rather than a self-serve public developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, reference documentation, or GitHub organization is available for catalog harvesting.

companies.name: Tuza
companies.description: Tuza is a banking automation platform that orchestrates AI agents, customers and workflows to eliminate the manual processes that slow banks down. Originally launched in the UK at tuza.co.uk as a card-payment fee comparison and switching service for merchants, the company has repositioned as Tuza AI, delivering agentic automation for banks. It is an early-stage, venture-backed fintech (backed by Northzone) building a product that connects AI agents with core banking operations and customer-facing workflows. As of this profile Tuza publishes a marketing and careers site only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface has been released yet, so this record captures verified company identity plus a domain-security probe.

companies.name: Vancity
companies.description: Vancity (Vancouver City Savings Credit Union) is a member-owned financial co-operative headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, and the largest community credit union in Canada, with over 543,000 members, roughly CA$35 billion in assets, and about 60 branches across the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island. Founded in 1946 as an open-bond credit union, it is provincially chartered and cooperatively governed, offering retail and business banking, mortgages, foreign exchange, Visa cards, insurance, and investment advice, with values-based and impact-lending positioning. Vancity exposes no first-party public developer API portal: developer.vancity.com and developers.vancity.com do not resolve. It participates in Canada's shared payment rails through Central 1 (its banking-technology and payments provider, including enhanced Interac e-Transfer real-time payments) and Payments Canada, while third-party consumer data access is provided through aggregators such as Plaid and Flinks. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework is legislated but not yet operational, so any programmatic account access today is voluntary and aggregator-mediated rather than served by a documented Vancity API.

companies.name: Amount
companies.description: Amount is a Chicago-based financial technology company that provides banks, credit unions, and fintechs with a digital lending and account-origination platform. Spun out of the consumer lender Avant in 2020 and backed by QED Investors, Amount delivers configurable software for personal loans, point-of-sale and buy-now-pay-later financing, deposit and account opening, and integrated fraud, identity verification, and decisioning. Its product API is delivered to enterprise banking customers through a private, credentialed developer portal (docs.amount.com) rather than a public self-serve API.

companies.name: First Horizon Corporation
companies.description: First Horizon Corporation (NYSE: FHN), headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, is a regional financial-services holding company operating across 12 southeastern U.S. states through its principal subsidiary, First Horizon Bank. The franchise reports roughly $84 billion in total assets, $67 billion in deposits, and approximately 410 banking centers as of Q1 2026. Business lines include consumer and small-business banking, commercial and specialty lending, private banking and wealth management, and FHN Financial fixed- income capital markets. The company was founded in 1864 as First National Bank of Memphis, rebranded as First Tennessee in 1977, became First Horizon National Corporation in 2004, and shortened its name to First Horizon Corporation following the 2020 IberiaBank merger. In February 2022 First Horizon announced a $13.4 billion all-cash acquisition by Toronto-Dominion Bank; the parties mutually terminated the merger on May 4, 2023, citing regulatory uncertainty around the deal's closing timeline, with TD paying a $225 million termination fee plus a previously agreed $25 million reimbursement to First Horizon. First Horizon does not publish a public developer API portal. Customer account data is reachable for fintech use cases only through US open-banking aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and through emerging Financial Data Exchange (FDX) APIs that will be required of covered data providers under the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule. Commercial APIs for treasury management, ACH origination, wire initiation, and host-to-host file transfer are available to corporate clients under direct contract through First Horizon Treasury Management Services but are not publicly documented.

companies.name: Manulife
companies.description: Manulife Financial Corporation is a Canadian multinational insurance and financial services company providing life insurance, health insurance, wealth and asset management, banking, and group benefits. Manulife operates under the Manulife brand in Canada and Asia and through John Hancock Financial in the United States, with Manulife Bank of Canada and Manulife Investment Management as key subsidiaries. The company is the largest insurance company in Canada and serves millions of customers worldwide. Manulife does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; partner integrations are managed through closed channels.

companies.name: PNC Financial Services Group
companies.description: PNC Financial Services Group is one of the largest diversified financial services institutions in the United States, organized around customers, communities, and employees offering retail and corporate banking, asset management, and residential mortgage services. This repository tracks APIs, SDKs, and other developer resources associated with PNC Financial Services Group.

companies.name: Old National Bancorp
companies.description: Old National Bancorp is a regional bank holding company headquartered in Indiana and a Fortune 1000 firm that provides consumer banking, commercial banking, mortgage, and wealth management services across the U.S. Midwest and Southeast. The bank operates branch and digital banking channels including mobile and online banking, bill pay, and Zelle. Old National does not publish a public developer portal or external open banking API.

companies.name: AND Global
companies.description: AND Global is a fintech-as-a-service company operating across the Asia-Pacific region, with offices in Mongolia, Singapore, Japan, the Philippines, and Thailand. It builds software that lets banks and lenders launch digital lending and financial products, integrating with banking and payment systems through APIs and other means. Its solutions span automated lending lifecycle management (Looms), custom and AI/ML credit scoring (Scorecard Builder, Custom AI Scoring, Niko AutoML), intelligent document processing (Mindox), omnichannel customer data, document management (DMS), and a collaborative investment platform (Oasis). Consumer-facing brands include the LendMN and Lend Pinoy digital lending platforms. AND Global was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; no public developer portal or API documentation was found at profiling time.

companies.name: Ballard Spahr
companies.description: Ballard Spahr LLP is a national U.S. law firm founded in 1885 and headquartered in Philadelphia. Following its January 1, 2025 combination with Seattle-based Lane Powell, the firm operates as a "nationally recognized firm of more than 750 lawyers across 18 U.S. offices" with departments in Business and Transactions, Finance, Intellectual Property, Litigation, and Real Estate. The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

companies.name: Fraudio
companies.description: Fraudio is an Amsterdam-based payments fraud detection and financial-crime scale-up founded in 2019 by João Moura (CEO), Nathan Trousdell (COO), and team, with additional offices in London, Lisbon, and Barcelona. Fraudio delivers AI- and machine-learning-driven fraud detection as a managed service to merchant acquirers, payment service providers, card issuers, and banks, with a product line that covers card payment fraud, merchant initiated fraud, anti-money laundering, authorised push payment (APP) fraud, and money mule detection. The company markets itself as "Generation 3" fraud detection, advancing past rule-based (Gen 1) and bespoke per-customer ML (Gen 2) approaches by training a single centralized "patent pending AI super brain" on the pooled transaction history of all of its customers, claiming network-effect performance gains versus single-tenant models. Fraudio integrates with customers through a plug-and-play real-time scoring API with sub-100ms response times, configurable risk-appetite thresholds, and no upfront integration or setup cost. Customers include Viva Wallet, Silverflow, Pismo, Bancontact, Fazz, PayTabs, IXOPAY, Bold.co, SaltPay, WiPay, ePayco, and LOQR. Fraudio is ISO 27001 certified, was selected for the Visa Innovation Program (2023), is co-financed by the EU Lisboa 2030 programme, has raised roughly $3.3M seed plus a Series A round (March 2025), and counts BigStar Ventures, BYND Venture Capital, Teya, Viva Wallet, Portugal Ventures, Iberis Capital, Shilling, and CTT among its investors. There is no public developer portal, no open API reference, no public OpenAPI spec, no SDK, and no GitHub organization — the fraud-scoring API is delivered as a gated B2B integration through a commercial sales process.

companies.name: Popular
companies.description: Popular Inc. is a financial holding company offering retail, mortgage, and commercial banking services through its principal subsidiaries Banco Popular de Puerto Rico and Popular Bank in the continental United States.

companies.name: Saris
companies.description: Saris (saris.ai) is an enterprise AI company building AI workflow agents for banks and credit unions. Its platform automates multi-step back-office processes across lending, compliance, and operations — document processing, data validation, core-system updates, and compliance tracking — while keeping humans in control with full audit trails. Saris integrates with financial-technology platforms such as Fiserv and with model providers including OpenAI and Anthropic, and is a recommended CCUA partner for Northeast credit unions. The company raised a $28.8M Series A and is backed by 8vc. As of this enrichment pass Saris exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Ualá
companies.description: Ualá is an Argentine financial technology company and neobank founded in 2017 by Pierpaolo Barbieri, headquartered in Buenos Aires. The company delivers a mobile-first financial ecosystem anchored by a Mastercard prepaid/debit card linked to an in-app account, with a layered product suite that includes credit cards, personal loans, savings accounts with yield, fixed-term deposits, mutual funds (FCIs), stocks, bonds, CEDEARs, insurance, bill payments, recharges, and international transfers. Its merchant arm, Ualá Bis, provides payment links, online checkout, and POS hardware (POS Mini and POS Pro) for SMBs and online stores, exposing a public Cobros Online v2 API plus SDKs and pre-built integrations for WooCommerce, Tienda Nube, Magento, and Empretienda. Ualá operates as a regulated bank in Argentina (under BCRA oversight), has acquired ABC Capital in Mexico to operate as a chartered Mexican bank, and is the first technology-based company licensed as a financing entity by Colombia's Financial Superintendence. The company reached a $3.2B valuation following $195M in new equity in 2024, and reports more than eight million users across Argentina, Mexico, and Colombia. UaláScore, the company's AI-driven credit evaluation system, powers personalized lending across markets. Public developer surface is limited to the Ualá Bis merchant payments API; the consumer banking, lending, and investing capabilities are not exposed as third-party developer APIs.

companies.name: Abe AI
companies.description: Abe AI was a conversational-AI platform for banks and credit unions, delivering a financial virtual assistant (chatbot and voice) across web, mobile, SMS, and smart-speaker channels so consumers could check balances, track spending, and bank by natural language. Founded in Orlando, Florida and backed by Techstars, Abe AI was acquired by Envestnet | Yodlee in 2019; its conversational-banking technology was folded into Yodlee's fintech data platform. The abe.ai domain now 301-redirects to yodlee.com/fintech/conversational-ai and no longer operates an independent developer or API surface.

companies.name: Alliant Credit Union
companies.description: Alliant Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). Founded in 1935 as the United Airlines Employees' Credit Union and rebranded Alliant in 2003, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with more than 800,000 members and over $19 billion in assets. Alliant operates as a digital-first, branchless institution offering consumer and commercial deposit accounts, high-yield savings and checking, credit cards, auto and home loans, and business banking. Like nearly all U.S. credit unions, Alliant publishes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned data access is available to members only through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API.

companies.name: Archer
companies.description: Archer (archermoney.com) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) financial-infrastructure startup building global payouts, stablecoin banking, and yield infrastructure for the companies powering the AI data economy. Archer lets data marketplaces, AI labor platforms, and reinforcement-learning environment providers onboard workers globally, pay contributors instantly with stablecoins, and earn yield on idle platform balances while funds remain on platform. The company aims to be the financial layer for the global workforce generating the data that trains frontier AI models, reducing cross-border payout costs and improving the financial experience for contributors. Founded by Benjamin Nguyen (CEO) and Vivek Yanamadula (CTO); early stage, no public developer surface or API specification published yet.

companies.name: Banksight
companies.description: BankSight Systems is a cloud banking software company founded in 2015 (San Francisco / Mumbai) that built an intelligent banking CRM and customer engagement platform for community banks, regional banks, and credit unions. The platform consolidated and analyzed customer data on top of Microsoft Azure and the Microsoft Power Platform, running a banking-specific data model with an open integration framework of pre-built connectors to core, LOS, and legacy banking systems, and delivered AI-driven "Next Best Conversation" recommendations to bankers and wealth managers. BankSight was acquired by Bottomline Technologies; its product now lives inside Bottomline's Commercial Digital Banking platform, and banksight.com 301-redirects to bottomline.com. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company (since exited) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Canadian Western Bank
companies.description: Canadian Western Bank (CWB) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank founded in 1988 (through the merger of the Bank of Alberta and Western & Pacific Bank) and headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta at Canadian Western Bank Place. Historically the largest publicly traded Schedule I bank headquartered in Western Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: CWB), it held roughly CA$43 billion in assets and focused on full-service business and commercial banking, personal banking, equipment financing and leasing, trust services, and wealth management across a network of affiliated entities. In June 2024 National Bank of Canada agreed to acquire CWB in an all-share deal valued at roughly CA$5 billion, and the acquisition closed in early 2025; CWB now operates as a subsidiary of National Bank of Canada and its branches and brand are being wound down and rebranded under National Bank. Consistent with Canada's voluntary and still fragmented open-finance landscape — the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework was legislated in 2024 (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the FCAC) but is not yet operational — CWB publishes no first-party public developer portal and no documented public API. Its developer and API hostnames do not resolve, and the entire cwbank.com domain now 301-redirects to National Bank of Canada (nbc.ca). Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid is confirmed via aggregator coverage directories). No first-party FDX-conformant data-access API was found. This is an honest identity-only, aggregator-only record for an institution now absorbed into National Bank of Canada.

companies.name: Dechert
companies.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

companies.name: Erebor Bank
companies.description: Erebor is a nationally chartered U.S. bank built for the next century of American innovation. Its digital banking platform serves businesses with FDIC-insured deposit accounts, ACH and wire transfer rails, batch payments, multi-party approval workflows, account statements, and identity verification delivered through a modern web application. Erebor was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass it does not publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or other machine-readable artifacts, so the profile is limited to verified identity and domain-security signals.

companies.name: Fenrock AI
companies.description: Fenrock AI is a Y Combinator (W26) company building specialized AI agents for the banking back office. Founded in 2026 and based in San Francisco by Charu Sharma and Michael M., Fenrock overlays on a bank's existing systems and ingests internal policies and standard operating procedures to automate compliance, financial-crime, and loan-operations workflows without requiring data migration. Its agents assist analysts with alert triage, case investigation, suspicious-activity-report (SAR) drafting, quality assurance, enhanced due diligence, KYC/KYB reviews, and sanctions/PEP monitoring, while preserving bullet-proof audit logs designed to pass regulatory examinations. Fenrock positions itself as an AI workspace that lets a single analyst process many times the volume of financial-crime and money-laundering cases. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record; Fenrock is an enterprise product company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: First West Credit Union
companies.description: First West Credit Union — rebranded Tru Cooperative Bank in 2026 — is a member-owned Canadian cooperative financial institution headquartered in Langley, British Columbia. Formed in 2010 by the merger of Envision Credit Union and Valley First, and later joined by Island Savings and Enderby & District Financial, it operates those four regional brands over a shared branch network with roughly 291,000 members, about $20.8 billion in total assets, 45 branches, and around 1,300 employees. After members voted in 2021 for federal continuance, it received a federal charter under Canada's Bank Act and became a federal credit union / cooperative bank (CDIC-insured) as of April 1, 2026. On the open-finance front First West / Tru runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or partner API; both developer.firstwestcu.ca and developer.trucooperativebank.ca resolve to nothing (NXDOMAIN). Third-party access to member account data today is aggregator-based (screen-scraping via providers such as Plaid and Flinks), the fragmented and voluntary Canadian norm while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) remains legislated but not yet operational.

companies.name: Florin
companies.description: Florin is a San Francisco fintech startup building an integrated financial operating system for venture-backed companies. Rather than reselling another bank's infrastructure, Florin is building the underlying money-movement rails end to end so that funds settle in real time on a single ledger the company owns. The product combines business accounts, cards, payments, and treasury management into one invite-only membership aimed at startup founders who would otherwise stitch together half a dozen separate tools to hold, move, and grow their capital. Florin was founded in 2026 by Shaurya Aggarwal (CEO), Amol Pant (CTO), and Aydin Sorensen, and is a member of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch. At the time of this profile Florin operates a single marketing landing page with a waitlist and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or other developer-facing surface yet; this entry captures the company's identity and awaits a public API to enrich further.

companies.name: Fortu
companies.description: Fortu (Fortu Wealth Ltd) is a London-based fintech, founded in 2019, offering digital private banking for high-net-worth individuals and their businesses, including borderless multi-currency accounts, payments, and a curated selection of investment opportunities across fintech and real-estate-driven debt strategies. Fortu also operates a business-to-business Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets private banks, wealth managers, and multi-family offices roll out their own branded investment and payments products, with automated payment processing and an API-driven compliance-monitoring tool. Co-founded by co-CEOs Firdavs Shakhidi and Azmat Sultanov, the company was selected for the 500 Global startup accelerator and raised an oversubscribed crowdfunding round (~GBP 500k) on Seedrs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Fortu does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, and its primary web deployment was offline (HTTP 402, disabled deployment) at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Gem
companies.description: Gem Security was a cloud detection and response (CDR) company, founded in 2022 in Tel Aviv, that built a real-time cloud threat detection, investigation, and response platform to shorten the time to investigate and contain cloud-native attacks. It raised roughly $34M from Team8, GGV/Notable Capital, IBM Ventures, Cisco Investments, and Silicon Valley CISO Investments, and was acquired by Wiz for about $350M in April 2024 to expand Wiz's CDR offering. Gem no longer operates as an independent product: the gem.security domain permanently redirects to Wiz and there is no standalone Gem developer portal, public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to enrich. This record is retained as an acquired-company / portfolio lead.

companies.name: Golden 1 Credit Union
companies.description: Golden 1 Credit Union is a state-chartered, member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Sacramento, California, and is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving roughly 1.1 million members across California with approximately 20 billion dollars in assets. Founded in 1933 and open to all Californians, it offers consumer checking, savings, credit cards, auto and home loans, and digital banking, and holds the naming rights to Golden 1 Center in Sacramento. Like most US credit unions, Golden 1 publishes NO public developer portal and NO first-party public API; its digital banking runs on a core-provider platform, and consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a documented first-party open-finance API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and this institution's public API surface is honestly empty as of this record.

companies.name: KaliSpot
companies.description: KaliSpot is a fintech network operated by Outsource Monetic Group Inc. (OMG), an Atlanta-headquartered startup with legal presence in Senegal and Morocco. KaliSpots are Financial Inclusive Service Points (FISP) — ATM and interactive teller machine (ITM) locations running a brand-agnostic, "phygital" infrastructure that bridges physical cash and digital financial services. From a single access point, customers reach banks, mobile money operators, and fintechs for 24/7 cash-in/cash-out (CICO), positioning KaliSpot as an independent omnichannel ATM operator across Francophone West and Central Africa, with pilots launched in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire. Founded 2021; pre-seed funding from 500 Global and Grenfell Holdings. No public developer API or documentation surface has been published to date.

companies.name: Khazna
companies.description: Khazna is Egypt's leading financial super app, a Cairo-based fintech building inclusive financial services for the country's underbanked payroll workers and their families. Through its consumer mobile app it offers earned-wage access and salary advances, bill and utility payments, savings, and everyday consumer lending, with the goal of extending affordable, digital financial services to people traditionally excluded from the formal banking system. Khazna is backed by Speedinvest and operates as a business-to-consumer application; it does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with verified public identity and domain-security signals.

companies.name: M&T Bank
companies.description: M&T Bank is a regional bank holding company that provides commercial and retail banking services to consumers and businesses across the eastern United States. As of the latest review, M&T Bank does not publish a public developer portal or open banking API; integrations are arranged through Treasury Management and commercial banking relationships.

companies.name: Manulife Bank
companies.description: Manulife Bank of Canada is a Schedule I federally chartered bank and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Manufacturers Life Insurance Company, part of Manulife Financial Corporation. Launched in 1993 as Canada's first branchless (direct) bank — and the first federally regulated bank opened by an insurance company in Canada — it operates entirely through online banking, a mobile app, and telephone banking, with no physical branches. It is best known for the Manulife One all-in-one account, the Advantage Account, GICs, mortgages, and lines of credit that connect everyday banking and borrowing with long-term financial planning. Manulife Bank publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; no developer.manulifebank.ca host resolves, and the public site is bot-protected. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework — legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer — is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer financial data access today is voluntary and occurs through financial-data aggregators (Plaid, Flinks, MX) rather than a first-party bank API. Interac e-Transfer is offered as a consumer feature but is not exposed as a documented public API.

companies.name: Monak E-Services
companies.description: Monak E-Services (Monak) is a fintech and lifestyle super-app serving working expats, travelers, and locals across the Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Oman). The consumer app bundles banking (local accounts, debit cards, remittance, and forex), health (medical visa, pharmacy, and insurance), and daily essentials (groceries, food, taxi, bill payments, and mobile/TV recharge), while a B2B side offers recruiters workforce onboarding and tracking software plus flight bookings, PRO services, and airport transfers. A 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation surface.

companies.name: Mountain America Credit Union
companies.description: Mountain America Credit Union (MACU) is a federally chartered, member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Sandy, Utah, founded in 1936 and regulated and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $21.9 billion in assets, more than 1.4 million members, and over 100 branches serving Utah, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, and Arizona, offering consumer and business checking, savings, mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and wealth services. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, Mountain America exposes no public first-party developer API or developer portal: there is no developer.macu.com or api.macu.com host, and every path under macu.com returns the same client-rendered application shell. Consumer-permissioned data access is intermediated through its core banking provider and data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a directly published API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and no public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented for this institution at the time of review.

companies.name: NEO Success
companies.description: NEO Success (operating as NEO Money) was a Bangkok, Thailand personal-finance and money-management fintech founded in 2019 by Punnamas Vichitkulwongsa and backed by 500 Global. It built a consumer platform aimed at helping users reach financial freedom and manage their money. As of this enrichment pass the company is out of business (per PitchBook) and its domain neomoney.com resolves to a parked domain-for-sale page (Afternic/GoDaddy) — there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

companies.name: NorthOne
companies.description: NorthOne was a mobile-first, API-enabled business banking platform for small businesses, freelancers, and startups, founded in 2016 by Eytan Bensoussan and Justin Adler with banking services provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. It offered the Connected Bank Account (a digital business checking account) with envelope budgeting, savings goals, bookkeeping and accounting integrations, cash deposits, and small-business lending, serving 320,000+ businesses and backed by Battery Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, and Tencent. As of 2026 the northone.com domain redirects to Relay (relayfi.com); NorthOne publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI.

companies.name: Open
companies.description: Open (Open Financial Technologies) operates at open.money as an India-based fintech offering a connected digital business banking platform for SMEs and startups. It pairs a business current account with invoicing, payments, automated accounting, expense management and payroll, letting founders run their banking and finance operations from a single dashboard. Open is a Speedinvest portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company website is protected by Cloudflare and no public OpenAPI could be harvested during enrichment.

companies.name: Oxygen
companies.description: Oxygen was a US fintech neobank founded in 2018 and a Y Combinator graduate, offering banking, debit-card, and financial products aimed at gig-economy workers, freelancers, small businesses, and entrepreneurs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company's consumer services are currently unavailable ("we are working on new and exciting initiatives") and no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface could be found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a company lead with a live web presence but no active API program.

companies.name: Paytm Payments Bank
companies.description: Paytm Payments Bank Limited is an Indian payments bank headquartered in Noida, offering digital savings and current accounts, the Paytm Wallet, FASTag, debit cards, UPI and other retail banking services to consumers and merchants. It operates as a distinct entity from Paytm's merchant payment-gateway developer platform (One97 Communications), and does not publish its own public developer API surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

companies.name: Rize
companies.description: Rize (Rize Money, Inc. / RizeFS) was a Banking-as-a-Service and embedded-finance platform that offered unified banking, brokerage, and payments APIs, letting companies embed savings, checking, and investment accounts directly into their own products. Rize was acquired by Fifth Third Bancorp in 2023; the standalone rizefs.com developer and API surface has since been decommissioned, with no live documentation, OpenAPI, or reachable endpoints found during this enrichment pass. The registered domain still publishes SPF and DMARC (reject) email records but serves no web or API hosts.

companies.name: Savedo
companies.description: Savedo was a German fintech operating a consumer deposit marketplace that let savers in Germany open fixed-term and savings accounts across multiple European partner banks from a single portal. Backed by Point Nine, it was acquired by Deposit Solutions in 2017 and is now a subsidiary brand of Raisin SE (WeltSparen). The Savedo customer portal was deactivated on 31 March 2022 and the brand no longer accepts new customers; existing balances are administered via flatexDEGIRO Bank AG. Savedo published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile is retained as a network lead surfaced from the Point Nine portfolio.

companies.name: Stori
companies.description: Stori is a Mexico City–headquartered fintech (operating as a regulated Sociedad Financiera Popular under CNBV and CONDUSEF oversight) on a mission to democratize credit access for the roughly 400 million underbanked consumers in Latin America. Founded in 2019, the company achieved unicorn status in 2022 and has raised over $400M from investors including GGV Capital, General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Goodwater Capital, Source Code Capital, Vision Plus Capital, BAI Capital, Tresalia, and GIC. Stori's flagship product is the Stori Card, an inclusive Visa credit card marketed to first-time borrowers with little or no formal credit history, alongside Stori Black (premium tier), co-branded cards (SHEIN, Farmacias Similares, sports teams), Cuenta+ (a commission-free deposit account advertising up to 15% annual returns), personal loans up to roughly $3,000 MXN-equivalent, and payment services covering bill pay, mobile recharges, and phone-based merchant collection. The platform is delivered exclusively through its iOS and Android mobile apps and serves more than five million Mexican users. Stori has no public developer API, SDK, CLI, webhook surface, or open-source release; its revenue model is interest, interchange, and fee income from consumer credit and deposit products, with operations in Mexico, Colombia, and a U.S. corporate presence in Arlington, Virginia.

companies.name: StreamLoan
companies.description: StreamLoan was a digital mortgage software company offering a point-of-sale (POS) and loan-origination platform that connected loan officers, borrowers, and real-estate agents to convert leads into funded home loans faster. Its toolkit spanned lead management, borrower communication and collaboration, workflow automation, document collection, security/privacy controls, and a branded borrower experience aimed at cutting the 40+ day mortgage close cycle. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - streamloan.io is parked on a registrar IP and every developer/app/api/docs/portal subdomain is unreachable (DNS records remain but no host responds), and no public API or developer program was ever documented.

companies.name: Suncoast Credit Union
companies.description: Suncoast Credit Union is a state-chartered, federally insured (NCUA), member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Tampa, Florida. Founded in 1934 as Hillsborough County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in Florida and one of the largest in the United States, serving well over a million members across Florida counties with more than $17 billion in assets. It offers consumer and small-business deposit accounts, lending, cards, and digital banking through a web presence (the brand's canonical domain is now suncoast.com, with the legacy suncoastcreditunion.com 301-redirecting to it) and an online/mobile banking platform hosted on banking.suncoastcreditunion.com. As is typical for a U.S. credit union, Suncoast publishes NO first-party public developer API and operates no developer portal: no developer or api subdomain resolves for either suncoastcreditunion.com or suncoast.com. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and its digital-banking core provider rather than a direct API. There is no publicly documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation and no published CFPB Section 1033 open-banking posture. This is an identity-only API Evangelist record reflecting an honest "no public API, aggregator-only" reality.

companies.name: Vyne
companies.description: Vyne was a London-based account-to-account (A2A) open banking payments platform, founded in 2019. It offered merchants real-time pay-by-bank payments, instant refunds, no-code payment links and verified payouts, built on open banking rails and real-time ACH networks with in-app biometric SCA across the UK and Europe. Vyne served retail, financial services and automotive merchants and won Best Open Banking Payments Project at the Open Banking Expo Awards 2023. In September 2024 Vyne was acquired by Dubai-based open banking platform Tarabut, and it wound down its UK operations effective 22 April 2025. The payvyne.com domain has since been repurposed to an unrelated site, and Vyne no longer operates a public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no live API to enrich.

companies.name: VyStar Credit Union
companies.description: VyStar Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida. Founded in 1952 as Jax Navy Federal Credit Union to serve military members at Naval Air Station Jacksonville and renamed VyStar in 2002, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $14 billion in assets, more than 950,000 members, and approximately 80 branches across Florida and Georgia. It is state-chartered and federally insured by the NCUA. Like most US credit unions, VyStar publishes no public, first-party developer API program: there is no live developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no documented first-party data-access API. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared with third parties through financial-data aggregators rather than a documented open API, and the United States has no single mandated open-banking contract. VyStar's open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, with the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule as the relevant regulatory horizon.

companies.name: Webfinanceholding
companies.description: Web Finance Holding AD is a Bulgarian financial-services holding company established in 2002 (formerly Finance Consulting AD). It specializes in the consultation and management of debt portfolios, acquisition of receivables, collection risk management, restructuring, and the management of enterprises in liquidation, and holds stakes across insurance, banking, and leasing subsidiaries including Saglasie Insurance, Texim Bank, and BM Leasing. The public web presence is a corporate and investor-relations site; no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is published.

companies.name: Webster Financial
companies.description: Webster Financial Corporation (NYSE:WBS) is a regional financial services company that delivers banking and financial solutions to businesses and individuals. The organization operates three business divisions - Commercial Banking, Consumer Banking, and Healthcare Financial Services - and manages over $75 billion in assets. Webster Financial does not publish a public developer API portal.

companies.name: Gain Credit
companies.description: GAIN Credit is a market-leading fintech providing responsible, AI-powered credit solutions for people underserved by traditional banks and lenders. The company combines deep financial expertise with advanced, AI-enabled credit-decisioning technology to offer affordable consumer lending, with funds disbursed within roughly 90 seconds of approval. GAIN Credit operates three consumer lending brands — Lending Stream, Drafty, and Afforda — serving the underserved credit market primarily in the UK, with operations across the US and India. Backed by QED Investors, Crosslink Capital, and Mohr Davidow. This corporate profile publishes no public developer API surface; it was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: MNT-Halan
companies.description: MNT-Halan is a Cairo, Egypt-headquartered fintech holding company and Egypt's first private fintech unicorn, founded in 2017 by Mounir Nakhla (CEO) and Ahmed Mohsen (CTO). MNT-Halan operates a financial super app ("Halan") and a vertically integrated digital ecosystem covering micro-finance and SME lending, consumer credit, e-payments and money transfers, an e-wallet, prepaid and installment cards, payroll advances, investment and gold-installment products, and e-commerce (electronics, appliances, FMCG, e-grocer). Lending products span nano loans up to EGP 2,000, microloans, consumer loans up to EGP 500,000 over 36 installments, SME loans from EGP 200,000 up to EGP 15 million, education and home financing up to EGP 4 million, light-vehicle financing, and buy-now-pay-later. The Halan app and its supporting agent network reportedly serve 5–7 million customers, have disbursed in excess of USD 4 billion in loans across 3 million borrowers, and process 100+ million USD in monthly payments and 50+ million USD in monthly e-commerce sales. After raising USD 400 million in 2023 to cross unicorn status and an additional USD 157.5 million in 2024 (including an IFC investment), MNT-Halan expanded beyond Egypt into Turkey (via the August 2024 acquisition of Tam Finans), the UAE (December 2024 launch), and Pakistan. MNT-Halan's revenue model is interest and fees on lending, merchant and payment fees, e-commerce gross margin, and card interchange; the company markets directly to consumers and SMEs through its Halan app and physical outlets, and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, partner sandbox, or open-source code repository.

companies.name: First National of Nebraska
companies.description: First National of Nebraska, Inc. is a privately held bank holding company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Through its subsidiaries, including First National Bank of Omaha, the company provides a full range of consumer, commercial, and agricultural banking services along with credit card processing and merchant services. It is one of the largest privately owned banking companies in the United States.

companies.name: New York Community Bancorp
companies.description: New York Community Bancorp, Inc. (now operating as Flagstar Financial) is a Fortune 500 bank holding company headquartered in Hicksville, New York. Through its banking subsidiary, the company provides commercial banking, multi-family lending, mortgage banking, and consumer banking services across the United States. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with the company. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

companies.name: Valley National Bancorp
companies.description: Valley National Bancorp is a regional bank holding company with its principal subsidiary, Valley National Bank, providing a full suite of commercial, business, and consumer banking services across the Northeast and Southeast United States. Valley National Bancorp does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

companies.name: Standard Chartered
companies.description: A British multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in London with a strong focus on Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Provides corporate, institutional, and consumer banking across more than 50 markets globally.

companies.name: Trumark Financial
companies.description: A Philadelphia-area credit union providing a full range of personal and business banking products and financial services to members across the region.

companies.name: Adjoint
companies.description: Adjoint Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts fintech (founded 2016) that built distributed-ledger and smart-contract software for corporate treasury and insurance. Its flagship platform, Uplink, let financial firms onboard assets onto a permissioned ledger, manage balances, and author self-executing agreements in Adjoint's Financial Core Language (FCL), with SDKs to bridge to traditional systems. The company raised roughly $10.4M and competed with Kyriba, Trovata, and Modern Treasury. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant: its adjoint.io domain now resolves to a parked/expired Namecheap page, its GitHub organization returns 404, and no first-party client SDKs are published to public registries. This profile is a VC-portfolio enrichment stub; see the data-quality note below regarding the originally-attached website.

companies.name: cashbus
companies.description: CashBus (现金巴士), operated by Micro-Credit Speed Express (Group) Co., Ltd. (微额速达集团有限公司) of Shanghai, is a Chinese mobile financial-technology platform providing quick microloans to underserved consumers who lack access to traditional banking. The company runs an automated, AI-driven credit decision engine that scores applicants in seconds using thousands of risk factors and big-data analysis, with risk management spanning pre-loan, in-loan, and post-loan stages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (company vision, team, careers, contact) with no published developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

companies.name: Cashforce
companies.description: Cashforce is a fintech platform focused on cash flow forecasting and working-capital analytics for corporate treasury and finance teams, connecting ERP systems, bank accounts, and financial data to give companies real-time visibility into cash positions, liquidity, and forecasting scenarios. Originally a Techstars-backed portfolio company, Cashforce was acquired by Billtrust and its standalone product surface is no longer independently operated; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public footprint. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definitions are currently reachable at the cashforce.com origin (the site returns HTTP 522), so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Hello Gold
companies.description: HelloGold is a Malaysian fintech company operating a mobile gold-savings app that lets everyday users buy, save, sell, send, and redeem 99.99% investment-grade gold starting from as little as RM1, with physical redemption from a minimum of 1 gram. Its SmartSaver feature runs an automated 12-month savings plan that buys gold at the lowest weekday price on the user's behalf. The service is Shariah-compliant (certified by Amanie Advisors), with gold stored in an insured and audited Singapore vault. HelloGold is a portfolio company of 500 Global and a recognized Islamic-fintech player. This profile is a consumer mobile-app company with no public developer/API surface identified during enrichment.

companies.name: Katch
companies.description: Katch is a Speedinvest-backed agricultural technology and embedded-finance platform serving agribusiness supply chains. It offers essential digital services for its partners, including e-commerce, grain procurement, and business intelligence, and layers embedded financial solutions such as factoring and credit directly within transactions. This lets agricultural partners manage cash flow, access working capital, and streamline supply-chain operations from a single platform. Katch was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, or machine-readable API surface for the company at this time.

companies.name: LittleFund
companies.description: LittleFund (styled Littlefund) was a New York City-based consumer fintech mobile app that let families create long-term savings and gift funds for their children. Instead of physical presents, relatives and friends could contribute money toward a child's fund for birthdays, holidays, and milestones, with funding from bank accounts or credit/debit cards and savings goals tracked in-app. The company was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) and was acquired by UNest, a children's investment and savings platform, around 2020. LittleFund operated as a B2C mobile product and never published a public developer platform, API, or documentation. Its original site at littlefund.co is offline and littlefund.com is now a parked domain; this record is retained as a historical company profile in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: RetailMeNot *
companies.description: RetailMeNot is a consumer savings destination that aggregates coupons, promo codes, cash-back offers, and deals from thousands of retailers and brands, helping shoppers in the United States save money when they buy online and in-store. It operates a website, mobile apps, and browser extensions that surface verified discount codes and cash-back at checkout, and it monetizes through retailer affiliate relationships rather than a self-serve developer platform. As of this profile RetailMeNot publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; probing found no reachable developer portal or well-known discovery documents, and partner activity is handled through whitelabel affiliate infrastructure.

companies.name: SeedFi
companies.description: SeedFi was a U.S. consumer fintech that offered credit-building loans and savings products (its "Credit Builder Prime" and "Borrow & Grow" plans) aimed at helping financially underserved borrowers build credit history and cash savings simultaneously. Backed by a16z and other investors, SeedFi was acquired by Cross River Bank in 2022, and its consumer offerings were subsequently folded into Credit Karma (Intuit). The seedfi.com domain now 302-redirects to a Credit Karma support article; SeedFi operates no independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained as a network company record with no API to enrich.

companies.name: Spenny
companies.description: Spenny is an Indian personal-finance and micro-investing app that works like a digital piggy bank, rounding up everyday spending on cards, UPI, and netbanking and automatically investing the spare change. Users can put round-ups and lump sums (from as little as Rs. 10) into digital gold and curated mutual fund baskets, with no lock-ins and anytime withdrawals. Spenny is a consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Tactic
companies.description: Tactic was a cryptocurrency and digital-asset accounting platform founded in 2021 in New York and backed by Lux Capital. Its product aggregated on-chain activity and exchange/custody data (Coinbase and others) into a unified treasury view and crypto sub-ledger, automatically categorizing transactions, calculating USD gain/loss and taxable events, and reconciling the crypto sub-ledger to traditional accounting software such as QuickBooks. Tactic launched from stealth in 2022 (originally on choosetactic.com, later the exact-match tactic.com) and raised roughly $13.6M before being acquired by TaxBit in January 2023 to augment TaxBit's digital-asset accounting suite. The standalone product, developer portal, and API surface have been retired; the tactic.com domain is now listed for sale and no independent developer surface remains.

companies.name: Bank of New York
companies.description: The Bank of New York was one of the oldest banks in the United States, founded in 1784. In 2007, it merged with Mellon Financial Corporation to form BNY Mellon (Bank of New York Mellon Corporation), which now operates as a global investments company providing asset servicing, treasury services, and wealth management. See the bank-of-new-york-mellon repository for current API documentation.

companies.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
companies.description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is a federal agency responsible for regulating and supervising national banks and federal savings associations. The OCC ensures that these financial institutions operate in a safe and sound manner, comply with applicable laws and regulations, and treat customers fairly.

companies.name: Capital.xyz
companies.description: Capital.xyz (the company behind the former Party Round) is a startup banking and fundraising platform that helps founders raise, hold, spend, and send money in one place. Companies sign up to run fundraising rounds, receive a virtual Visa debit card once capital is raised, hold and move funds, and connect the account to fintech services such as Gusto. The product is built on embedded-finance rails (Unit, Plaid, Visa) and is a consumer/SMB-facing application; as of this enrichment pass Capital.xyz publishes no public developer program, API reference, OpenAPI, or docs portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z.

companies.name: Clarity Money
companies.description: Clarity Money was a personal-finance and money-management mobile app founded in 2016 by Adam Dell (Oath Holdings / Dell family) that used data-driven analysis to help consumers track spending, cancel unwanted subscriptions, negotiate bills, move savings, and manage budgets. It was acquired by Goldman Sachs in 2018 and folded into the Marcus by Goldman Sachs consumer platform; the standalone Clarity Money app was subsequently discontinued. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. No public developer program, API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published, and the claritymoney.com domain no longer resolves to a live site (held by Goldman Sachs registrar CSC).

companies.name: Digit
companies.description: Digit was a consumer fintech company that built an automated personal-savings app: it analyzed a user's checking-account activity and quietly moved small, safe amounts into an FDIC-insured savings account, later expanding into automated investing and retirement (Digit Invest, Digit Retirement). Founded in 2013 in San Francisco by Ethan Bloch and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, Digit was acquired by Oportun in late 2021 and folded into Oportun's savings product. The standalone Digit brand is now retired: digit.co and hellodigit.com redirect to oportun.com/savings, and there is no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no active developer surface.

companies.name: Fincentric
companies.description: Fincentric Corporation was a Canadian core retail and wealth banking software vendor founded in 1984 and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia. It provided account processing, core banking, and wealth management technology to credit unions and financial institutions, serving roughly 167 clients worldwide and claiming a large share of Canada's top credit unions. Backed by Battery Ventures alongside BancBoston Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Shasta Ventures, and Ventures West Capital, the company was acquired by US core-banking vendor Open Solutions in May 2007; Open Solutions was itself acquired by Fiserv in 2013. Fincentric no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct entry — there are no API artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: Harvest Platform
companies.description: Harvest Platform was a New York City fintech startup founded in 2017 by Gabriel DellAccio and Namrata Baral that built a consumer investing and banking app. Its signature feature used artificial intelligence to identify negotiable bank fees and automatically negotiate refunds with major U.S. banks, later expanding into micro-investing, round-ups, cashback rewards, and savings tooling. The company was backed by Techstars and Financial Venture Studio, raising roughly $3.3M in seed funding. Its domain growmyharvest.com now 302-redirects to Acorns (acorns.com), consistent with reporting that Harvest Platform was acquired by Acorns in 2021. Harvest Platform was a consumer-facing mobile product and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so it carries no technical API artifacts.

companies.name: Ivella
companies.description: Ivella was a consumer fintech company that built shared money-management and multi-account banking tools aimed at couples and households, backed by the fintech venture firm Anthemis. As of 2026 Ivella's products have been sunset and the team has joined EarnIn to continue building. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Anthemis portfolio-company lead; the enrichment pipeline found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface, and the company is no longer operating as an independent product.

companies.name: Long Game
companies.description: Long Game was a San Francisco fintech startup founded in 2015 by Lindsay Holden that used prize-linked savings and casual mobile gaming to help Gen-Z and millennial consumers build healthy financial habits and grow their savings. Backed by Obvious Ventures and others (raising over $20M in venture capital), Long Game was acquired by Truist Financial in May 2022 and folded into Truist Foundry, which relaunched the Long Game app in May 2023. It is a consumer mobile product with no public developer API surface, and the standalone longgame.co domain no longer resolves.

companies.name: Maza
companies.description: Maza was an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) backed consumer fintech startup that helped Spanish-speaking and undocumented immigrants in the United States access the financial system - guiding users through applying for an ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number), opening a bank account, and obtaining financial services without a Social Security number. Founded in 2022, Maza raised an $8M seed round led by a16z in June 2023 and grew to more than 50,000 users. In April 2025 Maza was acquired by Flex for a reported $40M. Maza operated a consumer mobile application only and never published a public developer API, SDK, or event surface; following the acquisition its domains (maza.io, joinmaza.com, maza.us) now resolve to parked landing pages.

companies.name: Nostro
companies.description: Nostro refers to an account that a bank holds in a foreign currency at another bank (correspondent bank). Nostro account management involves reconciliation, liquidity management, and transaction tracking across correspondent banking relationships and multiple currencies.

companies.name: People's United Financial
companies.description: Defunct U.S. regional bank holding company, headquartered in Bridgeport, Connecticut. Acquired by M&T Bank Corporation in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $7.6 billion. The acquisition was announced February 22, 2021 and closed April 2, 2022. People's United operated roughly 403 branches at close and was fully integrated into M&T Bank by Q3 2022. The People's United brand has been retired; peoples.com now 301-redirects to mtb.com. No public developer program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, GitHub organization, or documented APIs existed at any point during its operating history.

companies.name: Ponto
companies.description: Ponto is a crypto banking and payments infrastructure company in the fintech sector, surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and Polychain and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be located for the company - the previously associated ponto.io domain now redirects to an unrelated party and no other candidate domain resolved to a live crypto-banking product. This profile remains a thin lead pending discovery of a verified developer/API surface, at which point the pipeline can harvest and enrich real artifacts.
